options.b: Its instruments are highly liquid and can be turned into cash quickly
options.c: Its instruments usually have maturities of five years or more
options.d: Its deals are usually large, wholesale transactions

questions.explanation: The money market deals in short-term instruments, generally maturing within one year, so maturities of five years or more belong to the capital market. Options B, A and D are genuine features of the money market: high liquidity, low risk and large wholesale deals.

questions.question: The money market is often described as a 'wholesale' and 'professional' market. This mainly means that

options.a: deals are usually large and dominated by institutional investors with specialised knowledge
options.b: instruments are sold only to retail savers in small units
options.c: only stockbrokers licensed by the stock exchange may buy or sell in it
options.d: all transactions must take place on a single physical trading floor

questions.explanation: Money market deals usually involve large sums with substantial minimum amounts, and the market is dominated by banks and other institutions that understand it. Option C describes dealing members of the stock exchange, while option B is the opposite of wholesale. Option D is wrong because money market dealing is not tied to one trading floor.

questions.question: The most basic distinction between the money market and the capital market lies in

options.a: whether the market is located in Lagos or in Abuja
options.b: whether the buyers are individuals or companies
options.c: the term and liquidity of the instruments traded, short-term and highly liquid in the money market
options.d: whether the instruments are issued in naira or in foreign currency

questions.explanation: The money market trades short-term, highly liquid instruments for adjusting liquidity, while the capital market deals in long-term funds for investment. Option D is wrong because both markets mainly deal in naira instruments. Options B and A are wrong because individuals and companies take part in both markets, and location does not define either one.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the money market and the capital market?

options.a: The money market deals in equities, while the capital market deals in Treasury bills
options.b: The money market finances factories and roads, while the capital market finances day-to-day cash needs
options.c: The money market is regulated by the SEC, while the capital market is regulated by the CBN
options.d: The money market mainly helps units adjust their short-term liquidity, while the capital market channels savings into long-term investment

questions.explanation: The money market exists mainly so that banks, firms and government can even out short-term cash surpluses and shortages, while the capital market turns savings into long-term funds for expansion and development. Option B reverses the two roles, and option A swaps their instruments. Option C swaps the regulators: the CBN oversees the money market and the SEC the capital market.

questions.question: While the Central Bank of Nigeria is the apex regulator of the Nigerian money market, the apex regulator of the Nigerian capital market is the

options.a: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
options.b: Debt Management Office (DMO)

questions.explanation: The SEC is the apex regulatory body of the capital market, approving and registering securities and supervising capital market operators. Option D, the NDIC, insures bank deposits and helps supervise banks. Option B, the DMO, manages government debt but does not regulate the market. Option C makes fiscal policy rather than regulating the capital market.

questions.question: Which group of institutions dominates the Nigerian money market, in the same way that non-bank financial institutions dominate the capital market?

options.a: Deposit money banks
options.b: Stockbroking firms

questions.explanation: Deposit money banks are the main lenders and borrowers of short-term funds, using the money market to manage their reserves and invest surplus cash. Options D and C take part but are more prominent as long-term investors and lenders in the capital market. Option B, stockbroking firms, are capital market operators who deal in shares.

questions.question: A merchant bank buys newly issued 182-day Treasury bills at the CBN's auction, and two weeks later sells some of them to a pension fund. The two transactions took place, in turn, in the

options.a: informal market and then the formal market
options.b: primary market and then the secondary market
options.c: capital market and then the money market
options.d: secondary market and then the primary market

questions.explanation: The primary market is where new securities are issued to raise fresh funds, as at a Treasury bill auction, while the secondary market is where existing securities change hands. Option D reverses the order. Option A is wrong because Treasury bills belong to the formal money market, and option C is wrong because both deals involve the same short-term instrument.

questions.question: Traders at a Lagos market each contribute N2,000 every day into a rotating 'ajo' scheme, and one member collects the whole pool in turn. In the structure of the Nigerian money market, this arrangement belongs to the

options.a: formal (organised) money market
options.b: discount market

questions.explanation: Esusu, ajo and similar traditional savings and credit schemes make up the informal money market, which is less regulated and less organised. Options C and B are parts of the formal market where banks and dealers trade with each other. Option A is the CBN-supervised segment, which an ajo scheme is not part of.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the formal (organised) segment of the Nigerian money market?

options.a: Esusu contribution clubs
options.b: The interbank market
options.c: Standing facilities operated by the CBN

questions.explanation: Esusu clubs are traditional savings arrangements and belong to the informal money market. Options B, D and C are regulated activities supervised or run by the CBN, so they belong to the formal, organised segment.

questions.question: In the Nigerian interbank market, banks

options.a: deposit customers' foreign currency with the Debt Management Office
options.b: buy goods on credit from one another using trade bills
options.c: borrow long-term funds from the public by issuing shares
options.d: lend to and borrow from each other to manage their daily liquidity, at rates set by supply and demand

questions.explanation: The interbank market lets a bank with spare cash lend it, often overnight, to a bank that is short, and the rate moves with the supply of and demand for funds. Option C describes raising capital in the capital market. Options A and B do not describe interbank lending at all.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the prerequisites for developing a money market?

options.a: A continuous and sufficient flow of assets of varying maturities
options.b: Availability of short-term funds whose owners are willing to invest them
options.c: A requirement that all instruments be listed on the stock exchange
options.d: A lender of last resort that guarantees the liquidity of the assets traded

questions.explanation: Money market instruments are mainly traded among banks and dealers, so listing on the stock exchange is not a condition for a money market. Options B, A and D are genuine prerequisites, along with intermediaries who pool funds and invest them in short-term bills.

questions.question: For a money market to work well, there must be an institution that stands ready to guarantee the liquidity of the assets traded by providing funds to banks when they cannot raise cash elsewhere. This institution is called the

options.a: lender of last resort
options.b: fiscal agent

questions.explanation: A central bank acting as lender of last resort supports the liquidity of money market assets, because banks know they can get funds from it in an emergency. Option C settles cheques and payments between banks, and option D arranges new share issues in the capital market. Option B describes a central bank acting for government in its financial affairs, which is not the same as backing market liquidity.

questions.question: Before the Central Bank of Nigeria was established, banks operating in Nigeria that had surplus short-term funds usually

options.a: deposited them with Nigerian discount houses
options.b: lent them to the Nigerian government through Treasury bills
options.c: sent them abroad for investment in the London money market

questions.explanation: Before the CBN existed, Nigeria had no money market, so surplus funds were repatriated overseas for investment in the London money market. Options B, A and D were not yet available: Treasury bills came after the CBN, and discount houses and CBN bills came decades later.

questions.question: One reason for setting up the Nigerian money market was to 'Nigerianise the credit base'. This meant

options.a: converting all foreign currency deposits into naira
options.b: restricting bank loans to Nigerian government agencies only
options.c: keeping funds in Nigeria to meet local credit needs instead of letting them flow to overseas markets
options.d: replacing all foreign bank staff with Nigerians

questions.explanation: Nigerianising the credit base meant giving local investment outlets to funds that would otherwise go abroad, so that they could meet the working capital needs of Nigerian businesses. Option D describes staff indigenisation, not credit. Options B and A are not part of the objective.

questions.question: Government revenue in Nigeria often comes in unevenly during the year while spending goes on all the time. The money market helps government deal with this mainly by

options.a: letting it fix the interest rates that banks pay depositors
options.b: letting it issue long-term development stocks to cover monthly salaries
options.c: letting it issue Treasury bills to bridge short-term gaps between spending and revenue
options.d: letting it sell shares in ministries to the public

questions.explanation: Treasury bills let government borrow for short periods and repay when revenue comes in, evening out seasonal swings in its cash flow. Option D is not possible, since ministries do not issue shares. Option B uses a long-term instrument for a short-term need, and option A is not a money market function.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a factor that helped the growth of the Nigerian money market?

options.a: The listing of Treasury bills on foreign stock exchanges
options.b: Laws allowing new and varied money market instruments to be created
options.c: The establishment and enthusiasm of the Central Bank of Nigeria
options.d: Government's policy of Nigerianising the credit base

questions.explanation: Treasury bills are domestic instruments issued through the CBN, and listing them abroad did not drive the market's growth. Options C, D and B are recognised growth factors, along with the teleprinter service and government's own financing needs.

questions.question: The introduction of the teleprinter service is listed as one of the factors that helped the Nigerian money market grow, because it

options.a: replaced Treasury bills with electronic money
options.b: speeded up transfers of funds between CBN branches and its head office in Lagos
options.c: allowed customers to withdraw cash from automated teller machines
options.d: allowed the stock exchange to trade shares online

questions.explanation: The teleprinter carried typed messages quickly, so bank transfers between CBN branches and the Lagos head office moved faster and funds could be put to use sooner. Options C and D describe much later electronic banking and trading technology. Option A is wrong because Treasury bills remained the main money market instrument.

questions.question: How does the money market give the CBN a ready gauge of whether funds are scarce or plentiful in the economy?

options.a: Through the number of new companies listed on the stock exchange
options.b: Through the number of bank branches opened each year
options.c: Through the volume of goods imported each month
options.d: Through movements in money market interest rates

questions.explanation: When funds are scarce, money market rates rise, and when there is excess liquidity they fall, so the CBN can read conditions from these rates. Option A reflects capital market activity, while options C and B are not direct measures of short-term funds.

questions.question: The function of the money market by which it sets benchmark short-term interest rates that reflect market conditions and serve as reference rates for other financial instruments is called

options.a: capital formation
options.b: price discovery

questions.explanation: Price discovery means the market itself sets the price of short-term funds, giving benchmark rates for other instruments. Option D refers to channelling funds from surplus to deficit units, and option C refers to shifting risk to others. Option A is the building up of long-term productive assets, mainly through the capital market.

questions.question: When a Nigerian bank's cash falls below the level it needs, its 'first line of defence' in the money market is usually to

options.a: sell its head office building
options.b: issue new shares on the stock exchange
options.c: discount its holdings of Treasury bills
options.d: draw on call money or borrow in the interbank market

questions.explanation: Call money and interbank funds are the quickest ways for a bank to raise cash, so they are its first line of defence. Option C, discounting bills such as Treasury bills, is the second line of defence, used when call money is not enough. Options A and B are long-term capital decisions, not money market liquidity tools.

questions.question: Bank A has already used up the call money and interbank funds it can raise, but is still short of cash at the end of the day. Its 'second line of defence' in the money market would be to

options.a: raise its own interest rates on loans
options.b: lend more money to other banks overnight
options.c: discount bills it holds, such as Treasury bills, for cash
options.d: buy more commercial papers from companies

questions.explanation: Discounting bills such as Treasury bills for cash is the second line of defence when call money and interbank funds are not enough. Option B would make the shortage worse, since lending uses up cash. Options A and D do not produce cash quickly, and buying commercial papers also uses cash.

questions.question: The CBN sells Treasury bills to banks through open market operations when it believes there is too much money in the banking system. The direct effect of this sale is to

options.a: increase banks' reserves and so inject liquidity into the system
options.b: reduce banks' reserves and so withdraw liquidity from the system
options.c: increase the amount of currency in circulation
options.d: raise the capital base of the banks

questions.explanation: When banks pay for the bills, money moves from their reserves to the CBN, so liquidity is withdrawn and the money supply tends to fall. Option A is what happens when the CBN buys securities. Option D is wrong because buying bills does not change a bank's share capital, and option C is the opposite of the intended effect.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a standard maturity of Nigerian Treasury bills?

options.a: 91 days
options.b: 270 days

questions.explanation: Nigerian Treasury bills are issued in maturities of 91, 182 and 364 days. 270 days is the upper end of the usual range for commercial papers and bankers' acceptances, not a Treasury bill maturity. Options A, C and D are all standard Treasury bill maturities.

questions.question: An investor who buys a Treasury bill and holds it to maturity earns a return that comes from

options.a: dividends declared by the Federal Government
options.b: the difference between the face value received at maturity and the discounted price paid
options.c: coupon interest paid to him every quarter
options.d: a share of the profits of the Central Bank

questions.explanation: Treasury bills are sold at a discount and redeemed at face value, so the holder's return is the gap between the two amounts. Option C describes a coupon bond, not a discount instrument. Options A and D are wrong because government securities do not pay dividends or profit shares.

questions.question: In which year were Treasury bills first issued in Nigeria by the Central Bank on behalf of the Federal Government?
questions.explanation: Treasury bills were first issued in 1960, under the Treasury Bills Act of 1959, soon after the CBN began operations. Option C is the year the CBN Act was passed, option D is when Treasury certificates were introduced, and option A is when certificates of deposit were introduced.

questions.question: Treasury certificates were introduced in Nigeria in 1968, mainly to

options.a: give commercial banks a way to lend to merchant banks
options.b: replace Treasury bills, which were abolished that year
options.c: finance the building of the National Theatre
options.d: widen the range of money market instruments and help finance the civil war and post-war reconstruction

questions.explanation: Treasury certificates were introduced in 1968 to add to the money market instruments available and to raise funds for the civil war and reconstruction. Option B is wrong because Treasury bills continued alongside them. Option A describes certificates of deposit, introduced in 1975, and option C has nothing to do with Treasury certificates.

questions.question: How did Nigerian Treasury certificates differ from Treasury bills?

options.a: They had longer maturities of one or two years and so offered higher returns
options.b: They had shorter maturities of 14 to 30 days
options.c: They were long-term equity instruments traded only on the stock exchange
options.d: They were issued by companies rather than by government

questions.explanation: Treasury certificates were Federal Government instruments like Treasury bills, but with maturities of one or two years and higher returns. Option D is wrong because they were government securities. Option B gets the maturity backwards, and option C wrongly makes them shares.

questions.question: Nigerian Treasury bills are sold to investors mainly through

options.a: an auction in which authorised dealers such as banks submit tenders on behalf of themselves and their customers
options.b: direct over-the-counter sales at Federal Ministry of Finance offices
options.c: a lottery among holders of savings accounts
options.d: a public offer of shares managed by an issuing house

questions.explanation: Treasury bills are issued on a discount basis through an auction-based system in which authorised dealers are invited to tender, and members of the public bid through these dealers. Option D describes how new shares are sold in the capital market. Options B and C do not describe how Treasury bills are issued.

questions.question: For a Nigerian deposit money bank, Treasury bills and Treasury certificates are regarded as

options.a: part of the bank's share capital
options.b: long-term risk assets similar to mortgages
options.c: fixed assets used in running the bank
options.d: primary sources of liquidity, because they can be turned into cash quickly

questions.explanation: Money market instruments such as Treasury bills and certificates count as primary liquidity, while loans and advances provide only secondary liquidity. Option C refers to buildings and equipment, and option A refers to funds contributed by shareholders. Option B is wrong because these government instruments are short-term and low-risk.

questions.question: A large, highly rated Nigerian food company needs N2 billion for 120 days to buy raw materials. It wants to borrow directly from pension funds and other investors, at a lower cost than a bank loan and without pledging any assets. The most suitable instrument is

options.a: commercial paper
options.b: a Treasury certificate

questions.explanation: Commercial paper is an unsecured short-term note that creditworthy companies sell at a discount directly to investors, usually more cheaply than a bank loan. Options B and C are government securities that a company cannot issue. Option D is issued by banks to evidence deposits, not by companies.

questions.question: What is the key difference between commercial paper and a commercial (trade) bill?

options.a: Commercial paper is secured on the issuer's assets, while a commercial bill is unsecured
options.b: A commercial bill is issued by the Federal Government, while commercial paper is issued by banks
options.c: Commercial paper has no maturity date, while a commercial bill matures in five years
options.d: A commercial bill arises from an actual sale of goods on credit, while commercial paper is not tied to any particular trade transaction

questions.explanation: Commercial bills come from business transactions, such as a buyer who cannot pay cash immediately for goods, while commercial papers are raised for general short-term funding and are not tied to a trade deal. Option A is wrong because commercial paper is unsecured. Options B and C misstate who issues these instruments and how long they last.

questions.question: A bankers' acceptance usually carries a lower credit risk than a commercial paper of the same maturity because

options.a: a bank has accepted it and so undertakes to pay it at maturity
options.b: it is secured by a mortgage on the holder's house
options.c: it is issued by the Federal Government

questions.explanation: Once a bank writes 'Accepted' on a bill, the bank itself is bound to pay at maturity, so the holder relies on the bank's credit rather than only the trader's. Commercial paper is backed only by the issuing company's reputation. Option C describes Treasury bills, and options D and B are not features of bankers' acceptances.

questions.question: Bankers' acceptances are used mainly in

options.a: paying monthly salaries of civil servants
options.b: raising equity capital for new companies
options.c: financing international trade, where an importer's draft is accepted by a bank

questions.explanation: A bankers' acceptance is a time draft drawn on and accepted by a bank, and it is used mainly to finance imports and exports because the seller can rely on the bank's promise to pay. Option D uses long-term bonds, and option B uses shares in the capital market. Option A is a payments matter, not trade finance.

questions.question: A bank formally accepts a time draft drawn on it, turning it into a bankers' acceptance, by

options.a: endorsing the back of the draft in favour of the CBN
options.b: stamping 'Paid' on the draft before it matures
options.c: writing 'Accepted' with an authorised signature across the face of the draft
options.d: crossing the draft with two parallel lines

questions.explanation: The drawee bank accepts by writing the word 'Accepted' on the face of the draft and signing it, which commits it to pay at maturity. Option A describes an endorsement, which transfers a bill, and option D describes crossing, which applies to cheques. Option B would mean the draft had already been settled.

questions.question: The holder of a negotiable certificate of deposit who needs cash before the certificate matures can

options.a: only wait until maturity, since it can never be transferred
options.b: demand that the CBN convert it into Treasury certificates
options.c: sell it to another investor in the secondary market
options.d: exchange it for shares in the issuing bank

questions.explanation: A negotiable CD can be traded, so the investor can sell it before maturity to another buyer. Option A describes a non-negotiable CD, which is held to maturity. Options B and D are not features of CDs.

questions.question: When certificates of deposit were introduced in Nigeria in 1975, they were designed mainly as

options.a: a way for the Federal Government to finance the civil war
options.b: an instrument for marketing boards to finance export produce
options.c: a share certificate issued by newly listed companies
options.d: an interbank instrument to channel commercial banks' surplus funds to merchant banks

questions.explanation: Certificates of deposit were introduced in 1975 as an interbank debt instrument, with merchant banks as the main issuers absorbing commercial banks' surplus cash during the oil boom. Option A relates to Treasury certificates of 1968, and option B relates to the produce bills scheme. Option C confuses a CD with a share certificate.

questions.question: Very short-term loans, usually overnight or for a few days, lent among banks and repayable on demand or at very short notice, are known as

options.a: call money
options.b: eligible development stocks

questions.explanation: Call money is lent for very short periods and can be called back at short notice, which makes it ideal for meeting immediate liquidity needs. Option B refers to government stocks close to maturity, option C to one- or two-year government securities, and option D to trade bills of about 90 days.

questions.question: Under the Call Money Fund scheme introduced in 1962, banks lent their surplus balances to the fund for investment in Treasury bills. The scheme was abolished in 1974 mainly because

options.a: the government's financial position had improved
options.b: banks were no longer allowed to keep balances with the CBN
options.c: the CBN had been shut down

questions.explanation: The Call Money Fund scheme was abolished in 1974 because the government's financial position had improved, so it no longer needed the scheme to fund its borrowing. Options C, D and B are wrong because the CBN, Treasury bills and banks' balances with the CBN all continued after 1974.

questions.question: A transaction in which a bank sells government securities to another party and at the same time agrees to buy them back at a set price on a set date is called

options.a: a bankers' acceptance
options.b: a rights issue

questions.explanation: A repo is in effect a short-term loan secured by the securities sold, with the difference between the sale and buy-back prices as the interest. Option A is a bank-accepted bill of exchange. Options D and B are ways of issuing shares in the capital market.

questions.question: How do CBN bills differ from Treasury bills in purpose?

options.a: CBN bills finance government budget deficits, while Treasury bills are used only to control inflation
options.b: CBN bills are issued by deposit money banks, while Treasury bills are issued by companies
options.c: CBN bills are long-term bonds, while Treasury bills are equities
options.d: CBN bills are issued by the CBN for monetary policy, to mop up excess liquidity, while Treasury bills raise short-term funds for the Federal Government

questions.explanation: CBN bills are the Central Bank's own instrument, used to withdraw excess liquidity from the banking system, though they look much like Treasury bills. Treasury bills are mainly a way for the Federal Government to borrow short-term. Option A reverses the purposes, and options C and B misstate what the instruments are and who issues them.

questions.question: Government development loan stocks are normally long-term, but those with less than three years left to maturity are counted as liquid assets of commercial banks when computing their liquidity ratio. Such stocks are called

options.a: Treasury certificates
options.b: stabilisation securities

questions.explanation: Development stocks close to maturity, with under three years to run, are called eligible development stocks and are accepted as bank liquid assets. Option B refers to securities the CBN directed banks to take up to reduce money in circulation. Option A refers to one- or two-year Treasury instruments, and option C to a savings instrument.

questions.question: The money market arrangement of the 1970s under which banks pooled their surplus funds with the CBN for investment, mainly in Federal Government stocks, was the

options.a: Bankers' Unit Fund
options.b: Produce Bills Finance Scheme

questions.explanation: The Bankers' Unit Fund pooled banks' idle funds with the CBN, which invested them in interest-yielding assets, mainly government stocks. Option B financed marketing boards' exports, and option D was the 1962 scheme for investing banks' surplus balances in Treasury bills. Option C is a modern CBN overnight deposit window.

questions.question: Under the Produce Bills Finance Scheme, which operated in Nigeria in the 1960s,

options.a: commercial banks lent their surplus balances to merchant banks through certificates
options.b: a group of financial houses discounted marketing boards' export produce bills
options.c: farmers deposited their harvests with the CBN as security for loans
options.d: the Federal Government issued long-term stocks to buy cocoa farms

questions.explanation: The Produce Bills Finance Scheme let a group of financial houses discount the bills that marketing boards drew to finance export produce, and it was abolished in 1968. Options C and D are invented arrangements. Option A describes certificates of deposit, introduced in 1975.

questions.question: Mrs Adeyemi places N5 million with her bank with no fixed maturity date. Either she or the bank can end the placement by giving seven days' notice, and interest is paid at an agreed rate. This placement is a

options.a: certificate of deposit
options.b: call deposit

questions.explanation: A call deposit has no set maturity and can be ended by either party on the agreed notice period, such as 24 hours or 7 days. Option D is placed for a fixed period, and option A is a certificate issued for a specified term. Option C is a cheque account that is repayable on demand without notice.

questions.question: When discount houses operated in Nigeria, their principal role in the money market was to

options.a: regulate stockbrokers and approve new share issues
options.b: insure the deposits of commercial bank customers
options.c: accept current account deposits and issue cheque books to the public
options.d: act as intermediaries between the CBN and licensed banks, trading in and holding Treasury bills and other short-term securities

questions.explanation: Discount houses traded in and held Treasury bills, commercial bills and other short-term securities, linking the CBN and the banks and helping the money market grow. Option C describes deposit money banks, and option A describes the SEC and the stock exchange. Option B is the role of the NDIC.

questions.question: The first discount house in Nigeria, which began operating in 1992 under CBN guidelines, was

options.a: Consolidated Discount Limited
options.b: First Securities Discount House (FSDH)

questions.explanation: First Securities Discount House, set up in 1992, was Nigeria's first discount house and later became FSDH Merchant Bank. Options D, A and C were also discount houses, but they came after FSDH.

questions.question: 'Information asymmetry' is listed as a problem of the Nigerian money market. This means that

options.a: instruments carry no information about their maturity
options.b: participants do not have equal access to market information, which weakens the efficiency of pricing
options.c: every participant has exactly the same information at all times
options.d: the CBN publishes too much information about interest rates

questions.explanation: Information asymmetry means some participants know more than others about market conditions, so prices may not reflect true supply and demand. Option C describes the opposite, equal information. Options D and A are not what the term means.

questions.question: Under the CBN's standing facilities, the Standing Lending Facility (SLF) allows

options.a: a bank short of funds to borrow overnight from the CBN, usually against eligible securities
options.b: companies to borrow directly from the CBN for five years
options.c: the Federal Government to borrow from commercial banks without interest
options.d: a bank with surplus funds to place them overnight with the CBN

questions.explanation: The Standing Lending Facility lets banks obtain overnight liquidity from the CBN when they are short of funds. Option D describes the Standing Deposit Facility, the matching window for banks with surplus cash. Options B and C are not CBN standing facilities.

questions.question: A pension fund buys 91-day Federal Government Treasury bills with a face value of N10,000,000 at a discount rate of 12% per annum. Using the bank discount method on a 365-day year (Discount = Face value x rate x days/365), what price does the fund pay?
questions.explanation: The discount is N10,000,000 x 0.12 x 91/365 = N299,178.08, so the price is N10,000,000 - N299,178.08 = N9,700,821.92. Option A uses a 360-day year instead of 365, and option D charges a full year's discount. Option B is the discount itself, not the price paid.

questions.question: Using the bank discount method on a 365-day year, what is the discount on a 182-day Treasury bill with a face value of N5,000,000 issued at a discount rate of 10% per annum?
questions.explanation: The discount is N5,000,000 x 0.10 x 182/365 = N249,315.07. Option A uses a 360-day year, and option D ignores the 182-day term and charges a full year. Option C is the price paid, N5,000,000 minus the discount, rather than the discount.

questions.question: Using the bank discount method on a 365-day year, what is the discount on a 364-day Treasury bill with a face value of N1,000,000 at a discount rate of 8% per annum?
questions.explanation: The discount is N1,000,000 x 0.08 x 364/365 = N79,780.82, slightly less than a full year's 8% because the bill runs 364 days, not 365. Option A treats the bill as a full 365-day year, and option C uses a 360-day year. Option D is the price paid, not the discount.

questions.question: An investor buys a 91-day Treasury bill with a face value of N1,000,000 for N975,000 and holds it to maturity. On a 365-day year, what is the investor's simple annual yield, calculated as (Face value - Price)/Price x 365/91?
questions.explanation: The gain is N25,000 on an outlay of N975,000, so the yield is 25,000/975,000 x 365/91 = 10.28% per annum. Option D divides by the face value instead of the price paid, which gives the discount rate rather than the yield. Option C is the 91-day return without annualising, and option A uses a 360-day year.

questions.question: Bank X lends N50,000,000 to Bank Y overnight (1 day) in the interbank call money market at 15% per annum. Using simple interest on a 365-day year, how much interest does Bank Y pay?
questions.explanation: Interest = N50,000,000 x 0.15 x 1/365 = N20,547.95. Option A uses a 360-day year, and option C charges a whole year's interest for a one-day loan. Option B misplaces the decimal point, giving ten times the correct figure.

questions.question: A bank lends N20,000,000 at call for 7 days at 10% per annum. Using simple interest on a 365-day year, what interest does it earn?
questions.explanation: Interest = N20,000,000 x 0.10 x 7/365 = N38,356.16. Option D uses a 360-day year, and option A is a full year's interest. Option B is the interest for only one day rather than seven.

questions.question: Bank P sells Treasury bills to Bank Q for N9,950,000 under a repurchase agreement and agrees to buy them back for N10,000,000 after 14 days. Using simple interest on a 365-day year, with the interest measured on the amount received (N9,950,000), what is the implied annual repo rate?
questions.explanation: The interest is N10,000,000 - N9,950,000 = N50,000, so the rate is 50,000/9,950,000 x 365/14 = 13.10% per annum. Option A measures the interest on the repurchase price of N10,000,000 instead of the amount received. Option B is the 14-day return without annualising, and option D uses a 360-day year.

questions.question: A company issues 90-day commercial paper with a face value of N2,000,000 at a discount rate of 14% per annum. Using the discount method on a 365-day year, how much cash does the company receive?
questions.explanation: The discount is N2,000,000 x 0.14 x 90/365 = N69,041.10, so the company receives N2,000,000 - N69,041.10 = N1,930,958.90. Option B uses a 360-day year, giving a N70,000 discount, and option C takes a full year's discount. Option A is the discount, not the cash received.

questions.question: The Lagos Clearing House is

options.a: a commodity market
options.b: an insurance underwriting centre
options.c: another name for the Lagos Stock Exchange

questions.explanation: A clearing house is where banks exchange the cheques drawn on one another and settle only the net amounts they owe each other, so the Lagos Clearing House is essentially a cheque sorting and settlement centre. Option C is wrong because a stock exchange is a market for buying and selling shares, not for clearing cheques, while Options A and B describe commodity trading and insurance, which have nothing to do with cheque clearing.

questions.question: The clearing system in Nigerian banking can best be defined as:

options.a: The writing off of bad debts by a bank at the end of the year
options.b: The process of paying cash over the counter to a customer who presents his own bank's cheque
options.c: The transfer of a customer's account from one branch to another of the same bank
options.d: The process by which banks exchange cheques drawn on one another and settle the net amounts owed, through a clearing house run by or under the Central Bank of Nigeria

questions.explanation: Clearing deals with cheques that are not in-house. A cheque paid into one bank but drawn on another has to be presented to the paying bank, so banks exchange such instruments at the clearing house and settle only the net balances through their accounts with the CBN. Cash paid on the bank's own cheque (B) and moving an account between branches of the same bank (C) happen inside one bank, and writing off bad debts (A) is an accounting matter.

questions.question: At the end of a clearing session, how are the net amounts owed between Nigerian banks settled?

options.a: By customers paying the differences directly to the other banks
options.b: By the NDIC paying the balances on behalf of the banks
options.c: By debiting or crediting the banks' settlement accounts with the Central Bank of Nigeria
options.d: By each bank sending cash in vans to every other bank

questions.explanation: Each bank keeps an account with the CBN. After cheques are exchanged, only the net position is worked out, and the CBN debits the banks that owe and credits the banks that are owed. Moving cash between banks (D) is exactly what clearing avoids. The NDIC (B) insures deposits and has no settlement role, and customers (A) have no part in inter-bank settlement.

questions.question: Under the manual cheque clearing system used in Nigeria before automation, cheques were cleared by:

options.a: Each customer taking his cheque to the paying bank in person
options.b: Posting all cheques to the Central Bank of Nigeria's head office in Abuja for payment
options.c: Scanning the cheques and sending their images electronically to a central computer
options.d: Representatives of the banks meeting physically at the clearing house to exchange cheques and work out their claims against one another

questions.explanation: In manual clearing, bank clerks met at the clearing house, swapped the cheques by hand and calculated who owed whom, and settlement was then made on their accounts with the CBN. The process was slow, and customers could wait many days for value. Electronic presentation of cheque data (C) came only with automated clearing, while B and A do not describe how clearing worked.

questions.question: Which of the following was a major benefit of introducing automated cheque clearing in Nigeria?

options.a: It abolished the use of cheques in Nigeria
options.b: It removed the need for banks to keep accounts with the Central Bank of Nigeria
options.c: It allowed banks to overdraw their accounts with the CBN without limit
options.d: It shortened the clearing cycle and reduced the clearing float, so customers got value for cheques faster

questions.explanation: Automated clearing replaced the slow, rowdy manual exchange with electronic processing of cheque data. Cheques cleared in fewer days, the float fell, and fraud and errors were easier to control. Cheques are still used (A), and banks still settle through accounts with the CBN (B). The new settlement rules were in fact designed to stop banks from overdrawing those accounts (C).

questions.question: The Nigeria Automated Clearing System (NACS), which handles electronic cheque clearing, is operated by:

options.a: The Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN)
options.b: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)

questions.explanation: NIBSS is the inter-bank payments infrastructure company owned by the CBN and the banks, and automated cheque clearing was moved to it and run through NACS. The NDIC (D) insures deposits, SEC (B) regulates the capital market, and the CIBN (A) is the professional body for bankers, so none of them runs cheque clearing.

questions.question: Financial institutions that are members of a clearing house, maintain accounts with the Central Bank and can participate directly in the clearing and settlement of cheques and other payment instruments are known as

options.a: clearing banks
options.b: microfinance banks

questions.explanation: Clearing banks are the banks that belong to the clearing house and settle inter-bank claims through their accounts with the Central Bank. Option D and option C describe banks defined by wholesale or long-term development financing, not by clearing-house membership, and option B refers to small community-focused lenders.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key characteristic of a clearing bank in Nigeria?

options.a: It is subject to strict CBN supervision
options.b: It is a member of the clearing house
options.c: It maintains a settlement account with the CBN
options.d: It is restricted to a single office in one locality

questions.explanation: A single office in one locality is the feature of a unit bank, not of a clearing bank, which typically runs a wide branch network. Options C, B and A are genuine features of clearing banks: settlement accounts at the CBN, clearing-house membership and strict regulatory supervision.

questions.question: Clearing banks maintain settlement accounts with the Central Bank of Nigeria mainly in order to

options.a: settle inter-bank fund transfers and net clearing positions
options.b: keep customers' valuables in safe custody
options.c: receive deposit insurance premiums from customers
options.d: issue currency notes on behalf of the CBN

questions.explanation: The settlement account at the CBN is where each clearing bank's net position after clearing is debited or credited, so inter-bank obligations are settled there. Option B is a service banks give customers, option D is the CBN's own function, and option C wrongly describes deposit insurance, which is handled by the NDIC.

questions.question: The organizational structure of a clearing bank is commonly examined at three levels. These are the

options.a: front office, middle office and back office levels
options.b: strategic, tactical and clerical levels
options.d: head office, branch and agency levels

questions.explanation: The three-tier view is governance (the board), management (executive management) and operational (departments and units). Option A is only the way the operational level is divided into front, middle and back office, and option D describes the branch network rather than the whole structure.

questions.question: The organ that sits at the apex of a clearing bank's structure and is responsible for its overall strategic direction and governance is the

options.a: Internal Audit Department
options.b: Board of Directors

questions.explanation: The Board of Directors is at the top of the bank's organizational structure and sets strategy and governance. Option C is the management level that implements the board's policies, option A is an operational control unit, and option D is not an organ of a bank at all, since depositors are creditors rather than owners.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the board of directors of a clearing bank?

options.a: Approving annual budgets and financial statements
options.b: Approving the risk management framework

questions.explanation: Processing account-opening forms is routine transaction work done by the operations department in the back office. Options B, C and A are all board functions: approving the risk framework, appointing and overseeing senior management, and approving budgets and financial statements.

questions.question: In the typical board composition of a Nigerian clearing bank, the Board Chairman is

options.a: a non-executive director
options.b: the Chief Financial Officer

questions.explanation: The chairman leads the board but is non-executive, keeping the oversight role separate from the day-to-day management led by the MD/CEO. Option C is wrong because the MD/CEO is the top executive and sits on the board as a separate member, while options B and D are executive roles.

questions.question: The board of Zenmark Bank Plc wants a committee to oversee financial reporting, internal controls and the work of the external auditors. This is the

options.a: IT Governance Committee
options.b: Audit Committee

questions.explanation: The Audit Committee oversees financial reporting, internal controls and the external audit process. Option D deals with approving large loans and credit policy, option C with executive pay, and option A with technology strategy and cybersecurity.

questions.question: A N25 billion facility requested by a cement manufacturer exceeds the approval limit of executive management and is sent to a board committee that reviews and approves large credit facilities and sets credit policies. The committee is the

options.a: Credit Committee
options.b: Risk Management Committee

questions.explanation: The board Credit Committee reviews and approves large credit facilities and sets the bank's credit policy. Option B is tempting because credit risk is a risk, but that committee monitors all categories of risk rather than approving individual loans; options D and C handle audit and board appointments.

questions.question: The Remuneration Committee of a bank's board is mainly responsible for

options.a: overseeing cybersecurity and digital transformation
options.b: monitoring all categories of risk facing the bank
options.c: determining compensation packages for executive management
options.d: handling board appointments and succession planning

questions.explanation: The Remuneration Committee decides the pay and compensation packages of executive management. Option D belongs to the Governance and Nomination Committee, option B to the Risk Management Committee, and option A to the IT Governance Committee.

questions.question: The chairman of a bank is due to retire next year, and a board committee is asked to identify a successor and review board membership. This task falls to the

options.a: Audit Committee
options.b: Governance and Nomination Committee

questions.explanation: Board appointments, succession planning and governance matters are handled by the Governance and Nomination Committee. Option C is tempting because it deals with directors' pay, but it does not choose who sits on the board; options A and D deal with audit and lending.

questions.question: The board committee of a clearing bank that oversees technology strategy, cybersecurity and digital transformation is the

options.a: Risk Management Committee
options.b: Executive Committee

questions.explanation: The IT Governance Committee is the board committee that oversees technology strategy, cybersecurity and digital transformation. Option A is tempting since cyber risk is a risk, but that committee monitors risk across all categories; option D covers financial reporting and controls, and option B is a management body, not one of the listed board committees.

questions.question: Which of the following best distinguishes the board of directors from executive management in a clearing bank?

options.a: The board sets strategy and oversees; executive management runs the bank day to day
options.b: The board is appointed by the CBN; executive management is elected by depositors
options.c: The board handles cheque clearing; executive management handles shareholders
options.d: The board runs the branches; executive management approves the annual accounts

questions.explanation: The board provides strategic direction and oversight, while executive management handles the day-to-day running of the bank and implements board policies. Option D reverses the roles, and options C and B are wrong because clearing is an operations task and neither the CBN nor depositors appoint these organs.

questions.question: The highest-ranking executive officer of a clearing bank, who implements board decisions, leads the management team and represents the bank externally, is the

options.a: Deputy Managing Director
options.b: Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer

questions.explanation: The MD/CEO is the top executive officer, responsible for the overall management of the bank and for carrying out the board's decisions. Option D is tempting, but the chairman is non-executive and leads the board, not management; option A assists the MD/CEO and option C gives legal and governance support.

questions.question: While the MD/CEO of a bank is on a two-week trip abroad, the executive who normally assists the MD/CEO and acts in his absence will be the

options.a: Board Chairman
options.b: Chief Operations Officer

questions.explanation: The Deputy Managing Director assists the MD/CEO and acts in his absence, often while overseeing specific business units. Option A is tempting, but the chairman is non-executive and does not step into the executive role, while options B and D head operations and compliance respectively.

questions.question: Foreign exchange operations, the investment portfolio and money market activities of a clearing bank are overseen by the

options.a: Executive Director, Treasury and Financial Markets
options.b: Executive Director, Retail Banking

questions.explanation: Treasury and Financial Markets handles foreign exchange, the investment portfolio, treasury operations and money market dealings. Option B manages branches and consumer lending, option C oversees corporate, commercial and SME banking, and option D is a control role for regulatory compliance.

questions.question: Which executive of a clearing bank is responsible for financial planning, accounting, financial reporting and investor relations?

options.a: Chief Risk Officer
options.b: Chief Operations Officer

questions.explanation: The Chief Financial Officer manages financial planning, accounting, reporting and relations with investors. Option A oversees credit, market and operational risk, option B oversees service delivery and process efficiency, and option C provides legal counsel and handles regulatory filings.

questions.question: Kemi is the officer who heads her bank's anti-money laundering and know-your-customer programmes and makes sure the bank obeys regulatory requirements. Her title is most likely

options.a: Chief Technology Officer
options.b: Chief Risk Officer

questions.explanation: Ensuring regulatory compliance, AML and KYC programmes is the role of the Chief Compliance Officer. Option B is the closest distractor, but the CRO oversees enterprise, credit, market and operational risk rather than AML/KYC; options A and C handle technology and finance.

questions.question: In a clearing bank, the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) is responsible for

options.a: branch network operations and consumer lending
options.b: enterprise risk management, including credit, market and operational risk
options.c: the core banking system and digital banking platforms

questions.explanation: The CRO oversees enterprise-wide risk management, covering credit, market and operational risk. Option C is the job of the CTO/CIO, option D belongs to a board committee, and option A is the Retail Banking executive's portfolio.

questions.question: In a clearing bank's operational structure, front office operations are best described as

options.a: units that process transactions and settle payments
options.b: units that recruit staff and manage facilities
options.c: revenue-generating units that deal directly with customers
options.d: units that check risk and enforce internal control

questions.explanation: Front office divisions such as retail, corporate and treasury are the revenue-generating units that win and serve customers. Option D describes the middle office (support and control), option A the back office (processing and settlement), and option B the support functions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a front office (revenue-generating) division of a clearing bank?

options.a: Corporate Banking Division
options.b: Internal Audit Department

questions.explanation: Internal Audit is a middle office (support and control) department that independently reviews controls; it does not generate revenue. Options A, D and C are all front office divisions that earn income from corporate clients, markets and high net-worth individuals.

questions.question: A bank's Risk Management, Compliance, Internal Audit and Credit Administration departments are grouped together as

options.a: back office (processing and settlement)
options.b: board committees

questions.explanation: These departments form the middle office, whose job is support and control: analysing risk, enforcing compliance, auditing and administering credit. Option C covers customer-facing earning divisions, option A covers transaction processing, and option B is wrong because these are departments, not committees of the board.

questions.question: The Operations Department, the Payment and Settlement Department and the Reconciliation Unit of a clearing bank belong to the

options.a: back office
options.b: front office

questions.explanation: These units carry out processing and settlement, which is the work of the back office. Option B is the revenue-generating side, option C is the control side, and option D refers to the board.

questions.question: A unit in a bank spends its day matching entries on its nostro and vostro accounts and clearing items stuck in suspense accounts. This unit is the

options.a: Reconciliation Unit
options.b: Treasury Division

questions.explanation: Account reconciliation, nostro/vostro account management and suspense account resolution are the work of the Reconciliation Unit in the back office. Option B is tempting because treasury trades foreign currency, but it deals rather than reconciles; options C and D handle loan documentation and letters of credit.

questions.question: An importer of generators in Kano asks her bank to process a letter of credit and handle the related trade documents. In a clearing bank's structure this work is done by

options.a: Trade Services in the back office
options.b: Marketing and Corporate Communications

questions.explanation: Letter of credit processing, bills for collection and trade documentation are handled by Trade Services, a back office unit. Option C reviews controls, option D sets executive pay, and option B manages the brand and public relations.

questions.question: Mr Adeyemi, a high net-worth businessman, wants investment advisory and estate planning from his bank. He will be served by the bank's

options.a: Reconciliation Unit
options.b: Commercial Banking Division

questions.explanation: Private Banking/Wealth Management serves high net-worth individuals with investment advice and estate planning. Option D serves small businesses and micro-finance, option B serves medium-sized enterprises, and option A is a back office unit that never deals with such clients.

questions.question: Mergers and acquisitions advisory, capital raising and underwriting are services of a bank's

options.a: Retail Banking Division
options.b: Operations Department

questions.explanation: Investment Banking provides M&A advice, capital raising and underwriting of securities. Option C is tempting since treasury deals in securities, but it focuses on foreign exchange, money market and asset-liability management; option A serves individuals and option B processes transactions.

questions.question: Credit appraisal, loan documentation, collateral management and credit monitoring are the functions of

options.a: Credit Administration
options.b: the Corporate Banking Division

questions.explanation: Credit Administration, a middle office unit, appraises credit, prepares loan documents, manages collateral and monitors loans. Option B markets and books loans to large corporates but does not control them, option C reviews contracts and recovers debts, and option D handles enquiries and complaints.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a support function in a clearing bank?

options.a: Human Resources Department
options.b: Payment and Settlement Department

questions.explanation: The Payment and Settlement Department, which runs clearing-house operations and inter-bank settlements, is a back office processing unit. Options A, C and D are support functions that serve the whole bank through staffing, vendor and facilities management, and brand management.

questions.question: Arranged from the top down, the hierarchical branch network of a typical Nigerian clearing bank is

options.a: head office, regional/zonal office, area office, branch
options.b: regional office, head office, branch, area office
options.c: branch, area office, regional office, head office
options.d: head office, branch, area office, regional office

questions.explanation: The head office sits at the top, regional/zonal offices oversee clusters of branches within zones, area/divisional offices supervise smaller clusters within a region, and branches serve customers. Option C reverses the order (bottom up), and options B and D jumble the levels.

questions.question: To reach traders in a village in Ebonyi State with no bank branch, a bank appoints a local shop owner to offer basic deposit and withdrawal services on its behalf. This arrangement is

options.a: agency banking
options.b: unit banking

questions.explanation: Using third-party agents to provide basic banking services in underserved areas is agency banking, which extends reach beyond traditional branches. Option C is a relationship between two banks, option D is control of several banks by the same persons, and option B is an independent one-office bank.

questions.question: In a clearing bank's branch network, a regional or zonal office

options.a: houses the executive management and central departments
options.b: oversees clusters of branches in a geographical zone and reports to head office
options.c: is an individual outlet serving customers directly
options.d: is a third-party outlet in an underserved area

questions.explanation: A regional/zonal office supervises a group of branches within a zone, such as a Lagos or Northern zone, and its regional manager reports to head office. Option A describes the head office, option D agency banking, and option C a branch.

questions.question: In organisational structure, line authority in a bank refers to

options.a: the right of specialists to advise managers without power to command
options.b: authority given to outside consultants and auditors
options.c: direct authority passed down the chain of command over people who carry out the bank's main business
options.d: authority held only by the board's committees

questions.explanation: Line authority is the direct, superior-subordinate authority that runs down the chain of command, for example from the MD/CEO through regional managers to branch managers, over the people doing the bank's core business. Option A describes staff authority, which is advisory, while options D and B wrongly confine it to committees or outsiders.

questions.question: The Legal Department of Union Star Bank reviews a branch's loan contract and advises the branch manager, but cannot order the branch to grant or refuse the loan. The Legal Department here is acting as a

options.a: board committee
options.b: line function

questions.explanation: Staff departments such as Legal, Human Resources and Research support and advise line managers but do not command them. Option B is wrong because a line function holds direct authority over the bank's main operations, while options A and C are unrelated organs.

questions.question: Which of the following officers holds a LINE position in a clearing bank?

options.a: A branch manager
options.b: The head of the legal advisory unit
options.c: An economic research analyst at head office

questions.explanation: A branch manager sits in the direct chain of command running the bank's core business of taking deposits and lending, so the post is a line position. Options B, D and C are staff positions that give specialist advice and services to line managers.

questions.question: The officer who has overall responsibility for running a bank branch, including business development, customer relations and approving loans within delegated limits, is the

options.a: company secretary
options.b: branch manager

questions.explanation: The branch manager heads the branch, is accountable to the area or regional office, and grants advances within the discretionary limits head office allows. Option C handles cash receipts and payments at the counter, option D reviews controls independently, and option A is a head office governance role.

questions.question: In a centralised bank, decision-making authority is

options.a: held by third-party agents in rural areas
options.b: shared equally among all banks in the clearing house
options.c: spread to branch managers, who decide most matters locally
options.d: concentrated at the head office, with branches referring major decisions upward

questions.explanation: Centralisation means authority is concentrated at the top, so branches refer major matters, such as large loans, to head office. Option C describes decentralisation, and options A and B do not describe internal authority within one bank.

questions.question: A branch manager in Ibadan must refer every loan request, however small, to head office in Lagos, and customers complain about weeks of delay. This problem shows a weakness of

options.a: the unit banking system
options.b: agency banking

questions.explanation: When all lending decisions sit at head office, branch managers lack authority to respond quickly and delays follow, which is a known drawback of centralised branch banking. Option C would give branches more local discretion and cut delays, while options A and B do not involve a head office controlling branches.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of decentralising authority to branch managers?

options.a: Elimination of the need for internal audit
options.b: Removal of the need for a clearing house
options.c: Tighter uniform control by head office
options.d: Faster decisions that respond to local customers' needs

questions.explanation: Decentralisation lets branch managers decide promptly and tailor decisions to local conditions. Option C is the strength of centralisation, not decentralisation, and options A and B are false because audit and clearing are still needed whatever the structure.

questions.question: A trend now seen in the organisation of clearing banks is the consolidation of back-office work into centralised processing centres and shared service models. The main aim is

options.a: ending membership of the clearing house
options.b: replacing the board with branch managers

questions.explanation: Consolidating back-office operations into central processing centres and shared services is done for efficiency, so processing is not duplicated in every branch. Options D, B and A are not the purpose of this trend.

questions.question: A banking system in which each bank operates as a separate entity, usually from a single office, with its own independent management and its operations restricted to one locality, is

options.a: group banking
options.b: chain banking

questions.explanation: Unit banks are independent, single-office banks confined to a particular locality. Option C uses a network of branches under one bank, while options A and B involve two or more banks under common control.

questions.question: Which of the following is a merit of unit banking?

options.a: It helps to prevent monopoly banking
options.b: It can easily grant very large loans
options.c: It attracts funds from many distant regions
options.d: It spreads risks across the whole country

questions.explanation: Because there are many small independent banks, unit banking helps to prevent monopoly in banking. Option B is a demerit in reverse, since unit banks have limited resources, while options D and C are merits of branch banking.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a demerit of unit banking?

options.a: Close personal relationship with local customers
options.b: Difficulty in meeting a sudden rush of withdrawals
options.c: Dependence on correspondent banks for remittance of funds

questions.explanation: A close personal relationship with local customers is a merit of unit banking, as it helps the bank mobilise funds. Options B, D and C are genuine demerits that come from the small size and single location of unit banks.

questions.question: Nigeria's commercial banks, such as those operating hundreds of outlets across the 36 states and the FCT under one head office, practise

options.a: unit banking
options.b: chain banking

questions.explanation: A single bank operating through a nationwide network of branches is branch banking, the system Nigeria practises. Option A is the single-office system popular in the USA, option B involves several separate banks controlled by the same persons, and option D refers to banks granting long-term industrial finance.

questions.question: Bank X suffers loan losses in its branches in a flood-hit state, but profits from its branches in other states cover the losses. This illustrates which merit of branch banking?

options.a: Freedom from holding company control
options.b: Quick local decision-making

questions.explanation: Under branch banking, risks are spread geographically, so losses in one area can be offset by profits made in others. Option D and option B are merits claimed for unit banking, and option A is unrelated to the scenario.

questions.question: Under branch banking, a branch does not need to keep large cash reserves for emergencies mainly because

options.a: the CBN guarantees every branch's withdrawals
options.b: customers must give notice before every withdrawal
options.c: cash can be quickly mobilised from sister branches
options.d: branches are forbidden to pay out cash

questions.explanation: A branch can draw cash quickly from sister branches of the same bank, so it can operate without holding large idle reserves. Options A, D and B are not features of branch banking and are simply false.

questions.question: Which of the following is a demerit of branch banking?

options.a: It makes efficient central bank control impossible
options.b: It restricts savings facilities to one locality
options.c: It prevents risks from being spread geographically
options.d: It can create oligopolistic and bureaucratic conditions in banking

questions.explanation: Branch banking concentrates banking in a few large banks whose branches are controlled by head office, which can produce oligopoly and bureaucracy. Option C and option A contradict its merits of spreading risk and allowing efficient central bank control, and option B describes unit banking.

questions.question: Multiple-office banking in which two or more banks, each keeping its separate name, are controlled by a holding company is

options.a: chain banking
options.b: group banking

questions.explanation: Group banking places two or more operating banks under a holding (parent) company, while each bank keeps its own identity. Option A is the closest, but in chain banking control is held by individuals through shares, not by a holding company; options C and D involve a single bank with branches or a deposit relationship between banks.

questions.question: Under group banking, the banks controlled by the holding (parent) company are called

options.a: operating banks
options.b: unit banks

questions.explanation: The banks under the holding company in group banking are called operating banks, and each keeps its separate name. Option C is the small bank in a correspondent relationship, option D is a clearing term for banks that settle on behalf of others, and option B is an independent single-office bank.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a demerit of group banking?

options.a: It may lead to monopoly
options.b: The holding company may divert surplus reserves to its non-banking interests
options.c: It allows operating banks to pool resources to finance large borrowings
options.d: The failure of one operating bank can affect others in the group

questions.explanation: Pooling resources to finance large borrowings is a merit of group banking. Options D, B and A are genuine demerits: contagion from a failing operating bank, diversion of funds by the holding company, and the risk of monopoly.

questions.question: Chief Okonkwo and his two brothers personally own controlling shares in three separate banks and exercise control through their proxies, without any holding company. This is

options.a: branch banking
options.b: unit banking

questions.explanation: Chain banking is control of two or more banks by the same individual or group of individuals through stock ownership, not through a holding company. Option D requires a holding company, option A is one bank with many branches, and option B is one independent bank.

questions.question: The main difference between group banking and chain banking is that

options.a: group banks share one name, while chain banks keep separate names
options.b: group banking involves one bank, while chain banking involves many banks
options.c: group banking is found only in England, while chain banking is found only in Nigeria
options.d: group banking uses a holding company, while chain banking is control by individuals through share ownership

questions.explanation: Both involve control of two or more banks, but group banking works through a holding company, while chain banking is control by one person or group of persons through owning stock. Option A is wrong because operating banks in a group keep separate names, option B is wrong because both involve several banks, and option C is false since both are common in the USA.

questions.question: In correspondent banking, the small bank in a small community that keeps deposits with a large city bank is called the

options.a: operating bank
options.b: respondent bank

questions.explanation: The small bank holding deposits with the city bank is the respondent bank, while the large city bank that holds those deposits is the correspondent bank. Option C reverses the two, option A is a group banking term, and option D is a clearing term.

questions.question: Correspondent banking is best described as a mechanism that

options.a: places two or more banks under one holding company
options.b: replaces the central bank as lender of last resort
options.c: lets a bank lend long-term to start-up industries
options.d: knits unit banks together through deposit relationships with larger banks

questions.explanation: Correspondent banking links independent unit banks into a network by having them keep deposits with larger city banks, so every bank is ultimately connected. Option A is group banking, option C is mixed banking, and option B is not a function of any commercial bank.

questions.question: The process of obtaining values for non-in-house cheques among deposit money banks, usually carried out at the clearing house of the CBN or its designated branches, is called

options.a: agency banking
options.b: the clearing system

questions.explanation: Clearing is the process by which banks exchange cheques drawn on one another and obtain value for them, traditionally at the CBN's clearing house. Option A is the use of third-party agents, option C is joint lending by banks, and option D is matching account entries.

questions.question: In the cheque clearing process of a clearing bank, which step comes immediately after branches collect cheques deposited by customers?

options.a: Sorting the cheques by paying bank into on-us and other-bank items
options.b: Settlement of net positions at the CBN
options.c: Holding the clearing session at the clearing house

questions.explanation: After collection, cheques are sorted by paying bank so that on-us cheques are handled internally and those on other banks go to clearing. Options B, D and C all come later: the clearing session, settlement, and customer notification are the final stages.

questions.question: Tunde pays into his account at Bank A a cheque drawn by his customer on Bank B. During sorting, the cheque will be treated as

options.a: an item for the Reconciliation Unit to hold in suspense
options.b: an item to be presented through the clearing house
options.d: a bill for collection handled by Trade Services

questions.explanation: A cheque drawn on another bank is not an on-us item, so it is presented to the clearing house for exchange with the paying bank. Option C applies only when the paying bank is the same as the collecting bank, while options D and A describe unrelated units.

questions.question: After a clearing session, the clearing banks settle with one another by

options.a: paying each cheque separately in cash at each other's branches
options.b: settling net positions through their settlement accounts at the CBN
options.c: having the NDIC pay the net debtor banks
options.d: sending each other's customers bank drafts

questions.explanation: Clearing is multilateral: after the session each bank's net position is worked out and settled through its settlement account at the CBN. Option A ignores netting, option D is not how inter-bank settlement works, and option C confuses the deposit insurer with the settlement system.

questions.question: In the clearing process, 'return items' are

options.a: unpaid cheques sent back through the clearing system with reasons
options.b: cheques drawn on the collecting bank itself
options.c: cheques that the collecting bank has refused to accept for deposit
options.d: funds sent by the CBN to settle net positions

questions.explanation: Return items are cheques the paying bank declines to pay, which go back through clearing with the reason stated, after which the customer is told. Option B describes on-us cheques, option D describes settlement, and option C never enters clearing at all.

questions.question: Magnetic Ink Character Recognition (MICR) technology was introduced into Nigeria's payments system mainly to

options.a: allow banks to keep accounts outside Nigeria
options.b: speed up machine processing of cheques and shorten clearing time

questions.explanation: MICR codes printed on cheques let machines read and sort them, facilitating document processing, shortening the clearing period and boosting public confidence. Options D, C and A are not aims of MICR; deposit insurance, for instance, is the NDIC's work.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the core objectives of the Nigerian Automated Clearing System (NACS)?

options.a: To significantly reduce the clearing float
options.b: To encourage the development of other electronic payment products
options.c: To abolish the use of cheques in Nigeria
options.d: To maintain and enforce standards for clearing procedures

questions.explanation: NACS was meant to process cheques more efficiently, not to abolish them. Options A, D and B are genuine NACS objectives, together with cost-effective processing of clearing items based on electronic data presentation.

questions.question: Under the Nigerian Automated Clearing System, an indirect participating bank differs from a direct participating bank in that it

options.a: does not need any account with the CBN
options.b: manages the NACS infrastructure
options.c: takes part in clearing through a direct participating bank
options.d: transmits clearing data straight to the Zonal Clearing House

questions.explanation: An indirect participating bank clears through a direct participating bank instead of sending data to the clearing house itself. Option D describes a direct participant, option B is the role of the Zonal Clearing House, and option A is wrong because both types kept settlement accounts with the CBN.

questions.question: Under the settlement framework the CBN introduced in April 2004, a bank that clears and settles cheques on behalf of other banks is called a

options.a: unit bank
options.b: respondent bank

questions.explanation: A settlement bank meets the conditions for direct participation and clears cheques on behalf of others, with non-settlement banks posting through it under an agency arrangement. Option B is a correspondent banking term, option A is a single-office bank, and option C is a group banking term.

questions.question: Under the April 2004 settlement framework, non-settlement banks were required to

options.a: deposit clearing collateral directly with the CBN
options.b: stop clearing cheques altogether
options.c: keep only operations accounts with the CBN and clear through an agency arrangement with settlement banks
options.d: keep settlement accounts with the CBN and clear for other banks

questions.explanation: Non-settlement banks kept only operations accounts at the CBN and had their clearing balances posted to a settlement bank's account under an agency agreement. Option D describes settlement banks, option A is wrong because only settlement banks deposited collateral directly with the CBN, and option B is simply false.

questions.question: Which electronic payment system in Nigeria lets a customer transfer funds to an account in another bank instantly, and is run by the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS)?

options.a: RTGS (Real-Time Gross Settlement)
options.b: MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition)

questions.explanation: NIP is the NIBSS instant electronic funds transfer system. Option A is the real-time system for individual large-value payments operated by the CBN, option C processes transfers in batches rather than instantly, and option B is a cheque-reading technology, not a transfer system.

questions.question: The key difference between RTGS and NEFT as used by Nigerian clearing banks is that

options.a: RTGS is run by agents, while NEFT is run by the NDIC
options.b: RTGS settles individual large-value payments in real time, while NEFT processes transfers in batches
options.c: RTGS is for cheques only, while NEFT is for cash only
