questions.explanation: On bankruptcy the customer can no longer operate the account, the bank should stop paying his cheques, and the bankrupt's property vests in a trustee in bankruptcy. Option C ignores the end of the customer's authority. Option A is wrong because the family has no claim, and option D is wrong because set-off may still apply to mutual dealings before the bankruptcy.

questions.question: In the bankruptcy of a customer who owes it an unsecured overdraft, a bank's normal remedy is to:

options.a: Seize any of the customer's property it chooses without court approval
options.b: Recover the debt from the customer's employer
options.c: Charge the debt to the customer's joint account holder's personal account
options.d: Prove in the bankruptcy for the debt and share in the distribution with other creditors

questions.explanation: An unsecured creditor proves its debt in the bankruptcy and is paid from the estate according to statutory priorities. Option A is wrong because, without security, the bank has no right to seize property. Option B invents liability for the employer, and option C ignores the rule that only accounts in the same name and right may be combined.

questions.question: In banking, a mandate is:

options.a: The bank's right to retain securities until a debt is paid
options.b: A court order freezing a customer's account
options.c: A letter from a referee confirming the customer's character
options.d: The formal authority given by a customer specifying who may sign cheques and operate the account

questions.explanation: A mandate tells the bank who may operate the account and how, for example which signatories must sign cheques, and the bank must follow it strictly. Option B describes a garnishee or freezing order. Option A describes a lien, and option C describes a reference.

questions.question: The mandate on the joint account of Tope and Yemi reads "BOTH TO SIGN". A cheque for N80,000 is presented bearing only Tope's signature. The bank should:

options.a: Pay it and ask Yemi to sign afterwards
options.b: Pay it, because Tope is one of the account holders
options.c: Pay it if the amount is below N100,000
options.d: Refuse payment, because the cheque does not comply with the mandate

questions.explanation: Under a "both to sign" mandate, a cheque signed by only one holder is not properly drawn, and a payment contrary to the mandate may not be debited to the account. Option B would fit an "either to sign" mandate. Options A and C invent exceptions that the mandate does not allow.

questions.question: One of the two holders of a joint deposit account, Mr and Mrs Nwosu, dies. Unless the account terms say otherwise, the credit balance normally:

options.a: Is shared equally between the survivor and the deceased's estate
options.b: Passes to the surviving account holder by the rule of survivorship
options.c: Is transferred to the bank's dormant accounts ledger
options.d: Is paid entirely to the deceased's estate

questions.explanation: Survivorship rules apply to joint accounts, so on the death of one holder the balance normally belongs to the survivor. Option A and option D ignore survivorship. Option C confuses death of a joint holder with dormancy, which arises only when an account is not operated for a long time.

questions.question: A formal written authority, signed and sealed, by which one person (the donor) empowers another (the donee or attorney) to act for him generally or in specified matters is a:

options.a: Bank reference
options.b: Power of attorney

questions.explanation: A power of attorney is the formal instrument by which the donor appoints an attorney (the donee) to act on his behalf. Option D is a customer's instruction to make regular fixed payments. Option C is a promise to compensate the bank for loss, and option A is a statement about a customer's character or standing.

questions.question: Alhaji Sani, who is travelling to Saudi Arabia for three months, signs a power of attorney authorising his son only to withdraw funds to pay the school fees of his younger children. This is a:

options.a: Specific power of attorney
options.b: Direct debit authority

questions.explanation: A specific power of attorney gives the donee authority for a stated purpose only, here paying school fees. Option D would allow the son to do anything the donor could lawfully do through an attorney. Option C concerns liability of joint borrowers such as partners, and option B lets a third party collect variable amounts from the account.

questions.question: On receiving a power of attorney from a customer, which of the following should a bank NOT do?

options.a: Allow the attorney to do anything he asks, even outside the powers listed in the instrument
options.b: Keep a certified true copy in the customer's file
options.c: Ensure that the power of attorney is stamped
options.d: Sight the original power of attorney

questions.explanation: The bank must conduct the account strictly within the powers listed in the instrument, so allowing acts outside them is wrong. Options B, C and D are genuine steps: the bank should see the original, keep a certified copy on file and confirm that the document has been stamped.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT revoke or end a power of attorney?

options.a: The bankruptcy of the donor or donee
options.b: The death of the donor
options.c: The donor expressly revoking the power
options.d: The donor's account receiving a large salary credit

questions.explanation: A salary credit has no effect on the attorney's authority. Options A, B and C are recognised ways a power of attorney ends, along with completion of its purpose, expiry of its time, mental incapacity of either party and implied revocation, such as the donor returning to run his own account.

questions.question: Three trustees operate a trust account for an orphanage in Ibadan. One trustee asks the bank to let him delegate his signing authority to his secretary. The bank should:

options.a: Refuse, because delegation of authority is not allowed on trust accounts and all trustees must sign
options.b: Agree, as long as he signs a letter of authority
options.c: Agree, if the other two trustees are abroad
options.d: Agree, because any account holder may delegate his mandate

questions.explanation: Trustees must act personally, so delegation of authority is not permitted on trust accounts and all the trustees must sign cheques. Options B, C and D all assume that a trustee may hand his authority to someone else, which the rule forbids, even though ordinary account holders may delegate in writing.

questions.question: Thomas Ude opens an account as guardian for his 12-year-old son, John Ude. How is the account normally titled and operated?

options.a: In the names of Thomas and John as a joint account, either to sign
options.b: In the bank's name, operated by the branch manager on John's behalf
options.c: In John's name alone, operated by John with his own signature
options.d: In the guardian's name with the words "IN RE" before the minor's name, operated by the guardian until the minor reaches 18

questions.explanation: A minor lacks contractual capacity, so the account is opened and operated by the parent or guardian, titled with the guardian's name followed by "IN RE" and the minor's name and date of birth, until the child is 18. Option C ignores the minor's lack of capacity. Option A wrongly lets a minor sign as a joint holder, and option B is wrong because the bank never operates a customer's account for him.

questions.question: When opening an account for a partnership, which of the following should a bank do?

options.a: Open the account in the firm's name and include a joint and several liability clause in the mandate
options.b: Require only one partner to sign the application, whatever the deed says
options.c: Open the account in the name of the senior partner alone
options.d: Obtain a certificate of incorporation and memorandum of association

questions.explanation: A partnership account is opened in the firm's name, with a mandate signed by all partners and a clause making them jointly and severally liable for its debts. Option C is wrong because the account belongs to the firm. Option D lists company documents, and a partnership is not incorporated. Option B is wrong because the application should be jointly signed by the partners.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT normally required by a bank when opening an account for a limited liability company?

options.a: The certificate of incorporation
options.b: A board resolution authorising the account and naming the signatories
options.c: The memorandum and articles of association

questions.explanation: A deed of partnership is the governing document of a partnership, not a company. Options A, B and C are standard company account-opening documents, which together show that the company exists, what it may do, and who may operate its account.

questions.question: The Igbobi Old Boys Association wants to open an account. In addition to the rules of the association, which document best shows that the members authorised the account and its signatories?

options.a: A certificate of incorporation from the Corporate Affairs Commission
options.b: A government gazette establishing the association
options.c: A certified extract of the minutes containing the resolution, signed by the Chairman (or President) and Secretary
options.d: A grant of probate from the High Court

questions.explanation: For clubs and societies the bank needs a resolution to open the account, evidenced by an extract of the minutes certified by the Chairman or President and the Secretary, plus the signatories' specimen signatures. Option A is required of companies. Option D is required for executors' accounts, and option B is required for government ministries and agencies.

questions.question: Barrister Oke is named executor in the will of the late Chief Adeyemi and wants to open an account to administer the estate. The key document the bank will require is:

options.a: A deed of partnership
options.b: A grant of probate

questions.explanation: Executors prove their authority to deal with a deceased person's estate by a grant of probate (or letters of administration where there is no executor). Option D is required of companies. Option A is for partnerships, and option C shows that a company exists.

questions.question: The regulatory process by which a bank verifies the identity, address and beneficial ownership of a customer before and during the relationship is called:

options.a: Commission on turnover
options.b: Status enquiry

questions.explanation: KYC requires banks to confirm who a customer is, for example through means of identification, BVN and proof of address, and to keep monitoring the account. Option A is a charge on current account debits. Option C is agreeing account records, and option B is a request for an opinion on someone's creditworthiness.

questions.question: Under KYC rules, enhanced due diligence is applied to which group of customers?

options.a: Every customer who requests a cheque book
options.b: All savings account holders below the age of 25
options.c: High-risk customers such as politically exposed persons (PEPs) and non-residents
options.d: Customers whose accounts have been dormant for six months

questions.explanation: Enhanced due diligence is extra scrutiny for higher-risk customers such as politically exposed persons, non-residents and those with complex ownership structures. Options A, B and D describe ordinary customers who receive standard KYC checks, not the enhanced checks applied for anti-money laundering purposes.

questions.question: Traditionally, which account requires the prospective customer to provide references from referees before it is opened?

options.a: Savings account
options.b: Fixed deposit account
options.c: Minor's savings account opened by a guardian

questions.explanation: References are traditionally taken when opening a current account because the customer will be issued cheques, which can be misused; savings accounts do not need them. Options A and B carry no cheque facility and so do not traditionally require references. Option C is also a savings account and likewise has no cheque book, so references are not traditionally required.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a current account from a savings account?

options.a: Only companies may operate savings accounts
options.b: A savings account can be overdrawn but a current account cannot
options.c: A current account is operated by cheques and attracts commission on turnover; a savings account uses withdrawal slips and does not attract it
options.d: A current account always earns more interest than a savings account

questions.explanation: Current accounts are designed for frequent cheque transactions and carry charges such as commission on turnover, while savings accounts use withdrawal slips or cards and are not charged commission on turnover. Option D is wrong because current accounts earn little or no interest. Option B reverses the overdraft rule, and option A is wrong because savings accounts are mainly for individuals.

questions.question: A foreign-currency account, such as one held in US dollars, used by Nigerian residents to receive foreign remittances and hold foreign exchange, subject to CBN regulations, is a:

options.a: Current account
options.b: Fixed deposit account

questions.explanation: A domiciliary account is held in a foreign currency and used for receiving remittances and trade payments. Option A and option B are naira accounts for transactions and term deposits respectively. Option C refers to any account that has not been operated for a long time, not a currency type.

questions.question: Her mobile network provider collects a different amount each month from Bisi's account for her post-paid phone bill under her signed authority, while her bank pays a fixed N20,000 monthly to her landlord on her instruction. These are respectively a:

options.a: Standing order and a direct debit
options.b: Direct debit and a standing order
options.c: Direct debit and a cashing credit
options.d: Standing order and a bank draft

questions.explanation: A direct debit lets a third party (the originator) collect variable amounts from the account, while a standing order is the customer's instruction to the bank to pay a fixed amount regularly. Option A reverses the two. Options C and D name instruments that do not involve regular payments: a bank draft is a single payment instrument, and a cashing credit lets a customer cash cheques at another branch.

questions.question: A bank gives a status report on a customer to a supplier who asked about the customer's creditworthiness. Which statement about such banker's opinions is correct?

options.a: They make the bank a guarantor of the customer's debts
options.b: They must disclose the customer's exact balance and all transactions
options.c: They can be given to anyone who asks, without any authority
options.d: They are usually given in confidence and without responsibility, but the bank must take care that the opinion is not misleading

questions.explanation: Banker's opinions are brief, confidential assessments given without responsibility, but careless or misleading opinions can still expose the bank to liability. Option B would breach secrecy, since opinions are general, not detailed statements. Option C ignores the need for the customer's implied or express consent, and option A confuses an opinion with a guarantee.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an agency function performed by a bank for its customer?

options.a: Making periodic payments such as insurance premiums
options.b: Collection of cheques
options.d: Buying and selling shares on the customer's behalf

questions.explanation: Accepting deposits is a primary banking function in which the bank borrows as debtor, not something it does as the customer's agent. Options A, B and D are agency services, because the bank acts on the customer's instructions in dealings with third parties.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid reason for a bank to close a current account that is in credit, after giving reasonable notice?

options.a: The customer has asked for a statement of account
options.b: The customer has refused to buy the bank's insurance products
options.c: The customer habitually draws on uncleared effects
options.d: The customer has kept a large credit balance for many years

questions.explanation: Habitually drawing against uncleared cheques is a recognised ground for closing a credit account, along with fraud-linked or negligent operation. Option D is a normal and desirable use of the account. Option A is a right of the customer, and option B is not a lawful ground for closure.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of the general procedure for closing a customer's current account?

options.a: Determining closing charges and the closing balance
options.b: Marking the ledger conspicuously "CLOSED"
options.c: Issuing the customer a new cheque book
options.d: Asking the customer to return unused cheques

questions.explanation: A closing account needs no new cheque book; in fact unused cheques must be withdrawn. Options A, B and D are all steps in closing an account: unused cheques are returned, charges and the final balance are worked out and paid, and the ledger is marked closed and recorded in the register.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: From the exporter's point of view, which method of receiving payment for exports carries the greatest risk?

options.a: Open account
options.b: Documentary letter of credit

questions.explanation: Under open account the exporter sends the documents of title straight to the importer and simply trusts him to pay later, so the exporter loses control of the goods. Option B is the safest because the issuing bank guarantees payment, option C at least keeps the documents under bank control until payment or acceptance, and option D means the exporter is paid before he ships.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: In a documentary letter of credit transaction, the bank that opens the credit in favour of the exporter is

options.a: the exporter's bank, known as the advising bank
options.b: the central bank of the exporter's country
options.c: the importer's bank, known as the issuing bank
options.d: the shipping company that carries the goods

questions.explanation: After the buyer and seller agree terms, the importer's bank (the issuing bank) opens the letter of credit in favour of the exporter. Option A is the bank that tells the exporter about the credit, not the one that opens it, option B plays no direct part, and option D carries the goods and issues the bill of lading but is not a bank.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Under a documentary credit, the exporter keeps control of the goods because

options.a: the goods remain in the exporter's warehouse until the importer collects them in person
options.b: the importer pays the shipping company directly before loading
options.c: the advising bank buys the goods from the exporter
options.d: the documents of title are released to the importer only against payment or acceptance of the bill of exchange

questions.explanation: The documents of title, such as the bill of lading, are handed over only when the importer pays (documents against payment) or accepts the bill (documents against acceptance), so the exporter is protected. Options A and B do not describe how the system works, and option C is wrong because the advising bank deals in documents, not goods.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A Nigerian bank keeps a US dollar account with a correspondent bank in New York to receive export proceeds and settle foreign payments. From the Nigerian bank's point of view, this account is

options.a: a vostro account
options.b: a suspense account

questions.explanation: Nostro means 'our', so it is the Nigerian bank's own account held abroad in foreign currency. Option A ('your') is an account a foreign bank keeps with a Nigerian bank in naira, option B is an internal holding account, and option C is a foreign currency account a customer opens with a Nigerian bank.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: An export arrangement in which the exporter ships the goods and sends the documents of title directly to the overseas buyer, relying entirely on the buyer to remit the proceeds after receiving the goods, is known as

options.a: documentary letter of credit
options.b: documentary collection

questions.explanation: Under open account the exporter hands over both the goods and the documents of title and simply trusts the importer to pay later, so the exporter loses all control. Option B still keeps the documents in the banking chain until the buyer pays or accepts, and option A adds a bank's undertaking to pay. Option D is a way of getting early finance on a bill, not a method of sending documents to the buyer.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: From the exporter's point of view, which international method of payment carries the HIGHEST risk of non-payment?

options.a: Open account
options.b: Documentary collection on D/P terms

questions.explanation: Open account is the riskiest for an exporter because goods and documents of title go straight to the buyer and payment depends only on the buyer's honesty. Option C gives a bank's guarantee of payment, and option B keeps the documents out of the buyer's hands until he pays. Option D is the safest possible position for an exporter, since the money arrives before the goods leave.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Which method of payment in foreign trade places the GREATEST risk on the IMPORTER?

options.a: Confirmed documentary credit
options.b: Documentary collection on D/A terms

questions.explanation: With advance payment the importer pays before the goods are shipped, so he bears the full risk that the exporter never ships or ships the wrong goods. Option D is the reverse case, where the importer receives goods first and pays later, and option B also lets the importer obtain documents before paying. Option A protects both sides, because the bank pays only against documents that comply with the credit.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A Kano exporter of sesame seeds hands his bank a bill of exchange drawn on a buyer in Germany, WITHOUT any shipping documents attached, and asks the bank to obtain payment. This is a

options.a: documentary credit
options.b: documentary collection

questions.explanation: When only the financial document, such as a bill of exchange, is sent for collection with no commercial documents attached, it is a clean collection. Option B would require commercial documents like the bill of lading and insurance certificate to accompany the bill. Option A involves a bank undertaking opened by the buyer's bank, and option C means the bank buys the bill rather than merely collecting it.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: In international trade, a documentary collection is best described as one in which

options.a: the bill of exchange is accompanied by commercial documents such as the bill of lading and insurance certificate
options.b: only the bill of exchange is forwarded to the overseas bank for payment
options.c: the exporter's bank buys the bill outright at a discount before it matures
options.d: the importer's bank gives an irrevocable undertaking to pay the exporter against compliant documents

questions.explanation: A documentary collection is a collection where the bill travels with the commercial documents, such as the bill of lading and insurance documents, and the bank releases them to the buyer only on payment or acceptance. Option D describes a documentary credit, which carries a bank undertaking that a collection does not. Option B is a clean collection, and option C is bill negotiation or discounting.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Which international method of payment is regarded as the surest for an exporter who wants a guarantee of payment from a bank, provided he complies with its terms?

options.a: Documentary letter of credit
options.b: Clean collection

questions.explanation: A documentary letter of credit gives the exporter a bank's guarantee of payment as long as he presents documents that comply with the terms of the credit. Option D keeps documents under bank control but the bank does not promise to pay, so the buyer may still refuse. Options C and B offer even less protection, because they rely on the buyer's willingness to pay.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Chief Adebayo, a Lagos cocoa exporter, needs cash now and cannot wait for his German buyer to pay. He endorses and delivers the bill of exchange drawn on the buyer to his bank, which pays him the face value less a discount for interest and commission. This service is

options.a: a standing order
options.b: bill negotiation

questions.explanation: In bill negotiation the exporter transfers the bill to his bank by endorsement and delivery and receives the face value less a discount, and the bank collects the full amount at maturity. Option D would mean the bank merely collects the money as agent and pays the exporter only when the buyer pays. Option C involves no bill passing through the bank, and option A is a domestic instruction for regular payments.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: An exporter negotiates a N4,000,000 export bill with his bank 3 months before maturity. The bank deducts interest at 12% per annum on the face value for the 3 months plus a commission of 0.5% of the face value. How much is credited to the exporter's account?
questions.explanation: Interest is N4,000,000 x 12% x 3/12 = N120,000 and commission is 0.5% x N4,000,000 = N20,000, so the exporter receives N4,000,000 - N140,000 = N3,860,000. Option C forgets to deduct the commission, and option B wrongly charges a full year's interest of N480,000. Option A deducts only the commission and ignores the interest.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A nostro account, from the point of view of a Nigerian bank, is

options.a: an account the Nigerian bank keeps with a correspondent bank abroad, usually in foreign currency
options.b: an account a foreign bank keeps with the Nigerian bank in naira
options.c: the account each bank keeps with the Central Bank of Nigeria for clearing
options.d: a foreign currency account opened by a Nigerian customer at a local branch

questions.explanation: Nostro means 'our', so it is our account held abroad: Nigerian banks keep these accounts overseas to receive export proceeds and settle foreign currency payments. Option B is a vostro account, which is 'your' account held with us. Option D is a domiciliary account, and option C is a settlement account with the central bank, not a correspondent banking account.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Accounts kept by foreign commercial banks with Nigerian banks, into which local-currency payments are made and from which the foreign banks settle their naira obligations in Nigeria, are called

options.a: domiciliary accounts
options.b: escrow accounts

questions.explanation: Vostro means 'your', so a vostro account is the foreign bank's account held with a Nigerian bank, used to settle obligations in naira. Option C is the opposite: a Nigerian bank's own account held abroad. Option A is a foreign currency account held by a customer in Nigeria, and option B is an account where funds are held pending fulfilment of a condition.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A Nigerian bank holds a US dollar account with its correspondent bank in New York and uses it to receive its customers' export proceeds. To the Nigerian bank, this account is its

options.a: domiciliary account
options.b: vostro account

questions.explanation: Because the account belongs to the Nigerian bank and sits with a bank abroad, the Nigerian bank calls it 'our account with you', that is, a nostro account. Option B is how the New York bank would describe the same account from its own side. Option A is a customer's foreign currency account in Nigeria, and option D refers to an account of a third bank, not the bank's own account.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: In a documentary letter of credit transaction, the issuing bank is

options.a: the importer's bank, which opens the credit in favour of the exporter
options.b: the bank that buys the exporter's bill at a discount before maturity
options.c: the exporter's bank, which tells the exporter that a credit has been opened
options.d: a bank in the exporter's country that adds its own undertaking to pay

questions.explanation: The issuing bank is the buyer's (importer's) bank, which opens the credit at the importer's request and gives the undertaking to pay. Option C is the advising bank, and option D is the confirming bank. Option B describes a negotiating or discounting bank.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: In a letter of credit transaction, the bank in the exporter's country that informs the exporter that a credit has been opened in his favour, without necessarily adding its own promise to pay, is the

options.a: confirming bank
options.b: issuing bank

questions.explanation: The advising bank is the exporter's bank that passes on (advises) the credit to the exporter and checks that it looks genuine. Option B is the importer's bank that opens the credit, and option A goes further than advising by adding its own undertaking to pay. Option D belongs to documentary collections, not documentary credits.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: In a documentary credit, the 'beneficiary' is

options.a: the shipping company that carries the goods
options.b: the bank that opens the credit on the importer's instructions
options.c: the exporter, in whose favour the credit is opened
options.d: the importer, at whose request the credit is opened

questions.explanation: The beneficiary is the seller or exporter who is entitled to be paid under the credit once he presents compliant documents. Option D is the applicant, option B is the issuing bank, and option A is the carrier, which issues the bill of lading but is not a party to the credit.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: The party who asks his bank to open a documentary letter of credit is known as the

options.a: advising bank
options.b: drawee bank

questions.explanation: The applicant is the buyer (importer) who requests the credit and agrees to reimburse the issuing bank. Option D is the exporter who receives payment under the credit. Options B and A are banks, not the trading party who requests the credit.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: An Aba shoe exporter is worried that the overseas bank that issued a credit in his favour may fail to pay. He asks a reputable bank in Nigeria to add its own definite undertaking to pay him against compliant documents. The credit has become a

options.a: confirmed credit
options.b: red clause credit

questions.explanation: A credit is confirmed when a second bank, usually in the beneficiary's country, adds its own undertaking to pay, so the exporter is protected even if the issuing bank or its country fails. Option C allows the credit to be passed to another supplier, option D restores itself for repeated shipments, and option B allows advances before shipment.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Under UCP 600, a documentary credit is

options.a: revocable by the issuing bank at any time before shipment
options.b: irrevocable, even if it does not say so
options.c: revocable unless it expressly states that it is irrevocable
options.d: irrevocable only if it has been confirmed by a second bank

questions.explanation: UCP 600 states that a credit is irrevocable even if there is no indication to that effect, so it cannot be amended or cancelled without the agreement of the issuing bank, any confirming bank and the beneficiary. Options C and A reflect older thinking about revocable credits, which UCP 600 no longer treats as the default. Option D confuses irrevocability with confirmation, which is a separate, extra undertaking.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: An irrevocable documentary credit is one that

options.a: can be cancelled by the importer once the goods have been shipped
options.b: allows the exporter to transfer it to another supplier
options.c: must always carry the guarantee of a second bank in the exporter's country
options.d: cannot be amended or cancelled without the agreement of the issuing bank, any confirming bank and the beneficiary

questions.explanation: Irrevocable means the issuing bank's promise cannot be withdrawn or changed on its own: the beneficiary (and any confirming bank) must agree. Option A would defeat the whole purpose of the credit. Option C describes a confirmed credit, and option B describes a transferable credit.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A Port Harcourt importer's bank receives documents under a letter of credit that comply exactly with its terms. The importer then complains that the goods, still at sea, may be of poor quality, and asks the bank not to pay. Under UCP 600, the bank should

options.a: return the documents to the exporter and cancel the credit
options.b: pay, because banks deal with documents and not with the goods
options.c: pay only half the value until the quality dispute is settled
options.d: refuse to pay until the importer has inspected the goods

questions.explanation: Under UCP 600 banks deal with documents, not with the goods or services to which the documents relate, so a complying presentation must be honoured; a quality dispute is a matter between buyer and seller under their sales contract. Options D and C would make the bank a judge of the goods, which it is not. Option A is impossible because an irrevocable credit cannot be cancelled without the beneficiary's consent.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: The internationally accepted rules that govern documentary letters of credit, published by the International Chamber of Commerce, are known as

options.a: Incoterms
options.b: The Bills of Exchange Act
options.d: UCP 600 (Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits)

questions.explanation: UCP 600 is the ICC's set of rules for documentary credits, the 2007 revision. Option C is the ICC set for documentary collections, not credits. Option A defines delivery terms such as FOB and CIF between buyer and seller, and option B is national legislation on negotiable instruments.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A Nigerian bank handling a documentary collection for an exporter would normally process it under which set of ICC rules?

options.a: ISP98
options.b: UCP 600

questions.explanation: URC 522, the Uniform Rules for Collections, is the ICC set that governs documentary and clean collections. Option B governs documentary credits, and option A is designed for standby letters of credit. Option D sets out delivery and cost-sharing terms between buyer and seller, not bank collection procedures.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: The main difference between documents against payment (D/P) and documents against acceptance (D/A) in a documentary collection is that

options.a: under D/P a bank guarantees payment, while under D/A no bank is involved
options.b: under D/P the buyer gets the documents only on paying, while under D/A he gets them on accepting a bill payable later
options.c: under D/P the bill is payable at a future date, while under D/A it is payable at sight
options.d: D/P is used only for imports, while D/A is used only for exports

questions.explanation: With D/P the collecting bank releases the shipping documents only when the buyer pays, usually at sight; with D/A it releases them when the buyer accepts a usance (time) bill, so payment comes later. Option A is wrong because neither D/P nor D/A carries a bank guarantee, as both are collections. Option C reverses the usual pattern, and option D is not a real distinction.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Under a documentary collection, an importer in Onitsha accepts a 90-day bill of exchange, collects the shipping documents and clears the goods, but at maturity refuses to pay. The exporter suffered this loss mainly because the collection was on

options.a: documents against payment (D/P) terms
options.b: documents against acceptance (D/A) terms

questions.explanation: Under D/A the documents, and so the goods, are released once the buyer accepts the bill, leaving the exporter holding only an accepted bill if the buyer later defaults. Under option A the buyer could not have obtained the documents without paying first. Option C would have given a bank's promise to pay, and option D means the money would have been received before shipment.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a documentary collection from a documentary credit?

options.a: A collection is governed by UCP 600, whereas a credit is governed by URC 522
options.b: In a collection the banks act only as agents and give no undertaking to pay, whereas in a credit the issuing bank undertakes to pay
options.c: In a collection the importer's bank guarantees payment, whereas in a credit only the exporter's bank is involved
options.d: In a collection the documents go directly to the importer, whereas in a credit they go through the banks

questions.explanation: In a collection the banks merely handle documents on the exporter's instructions and do not promise to pay, which is why a collection is riskier for the exporter than a credit. Option C gets the guarantee backwards, and option A swaps the two sets of ICC rules. Option D is wrong because documents pass through the banks in both methods; it is open account where they go directly to the buyer.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: In a documentary collection, the exporter's bank, which receives the documents from the exporter and sends them to a bank in the importer's country, is called the

options.a: confirming bank
options.b: remitting bank

questions.explanation: The remitting bank is the bank to which the principal (exporter) entrusts the collection, and it forwards the documents abroad. Option D is the bank in the buyer's country that actually presents the documents to the drawee. Options C and A are parties to documentary credits, not collections.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A sight letter of credit differs from a usance (term) letter of credit in that

options.a: a sight credit needs no documents, while a usance credit requires shipping documents
options.b: a sight credit is revocable, while a usance credit is always irrevocable
options.c: a sight credit can be transferred to a second beneficiary, while a usance credit cannot
options.d: under a sight credit payment is made when compliant documents are presented, while under a usance credit payment is made at a stated future date

questions.explanation: Sight means payment on presentation of complying documents; usance means the exporter is paid later, for example 90 days after sight or after the bill of lading date. Option B confuses timing with revocability, and option C confuses it with transferability. Option A is wrong because both are documentary credits that require documents.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Mrs Ezenwa, a Lagos middleman, holds a letter of credit from a Ghanaian buyer for 500 cartons of textiles. She has no stock, so she asks her bank to pass part of the credit to the Kano factory that will actually supply the goods. The type of credit that allows this is a

options.a: transferable credit
options.b: red clause credit

questions.explanation: A transferable credit allows the first beneficiary, usually a middleman, to transfer all or part of it to one or more second beneficiaries such as the real supplier. Option D renews itself for repeated shipments, option B lets the beneficiary draw an advance before shipment, and option C acts as a guarantee that is drawn only on default.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A back-to-back letter of credit is one in which

options.a: a middleman uses a credit received from his buyer as security to have a second credit opened in favour of his own supplier
options.b: the beneficiary transfers part of the original credit directly to a second beneficiary
options.c: the beneficiary can draw an advance before shipping the goods
options.d: the amount of the credit is automatically reinstated after each shipment

questions.explanation: In a back-to-back arrangement the middleman's bank opens a separate, new credit for the supplier, backed by the original credit the middleman received. Option B describes a transferable credit, where the original credit itself is passed on. Option D is a revolving credit and option C is a red clause credit.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A letter of credit contains a special clause allowing the exporter to draw an advance from the advising bank before shipment, to buy and pack the goods. This is a

options.a: standby credit
options.b: back-to-back credit

questions.explanation: A red clause credit, so named because the clause was traditionally written in red ink, allows the beneficiary to obtain pre-shipment advances, making it a form of pre-shipment finance. Option C renews itself for repeated shipments, option A is drawn only if the applicant defaults, and option B is a second credit backed by an original one.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A Lagos manufacturer imports the same raw material from India every month. Instead of opening a new credit for each shipment, his bank opens one credit whose amount is restored after each drawing for an agreed period. This is a

options.a: revolving credit
options.b: transferable credit

questions.explanation: A revolving credit is reinstated to its original amount after use, so it suits regular, repeated shipments between the same parties. Option B allows a middleman to pass the credit to a supplier, option C provides advances before shipment, and option D uses one credit to support another.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A standby letter of credit is mainly used

options.a: as the normal channel through which every shipment is paid for
options.b: to give the exporter an advance before the goods are shipped
options.c: to allow a middleman to transfer the credit to his supplier
options.d: as a guarantee, paid out only if the applicant fails to perform or pay as agreed

questions.explanation: A standby credit works like a bank guarantee: the beneficiary draws on it only when the applicant defaults, so in a smooth transaction it is never used. Option A describes an ordinary commercial credit, option B a red clause credit, and option C a transferable credit.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of a bill of lading?

options.a: It certifies the country in which the goods were produced
options.b: It is a document of title to the goods
options.c: It is a receipt for the goods issued by the shipping company
options.d: It is evidence of the contract of carriage

questions.explanation: A bill of lading performs three classic functions: it is a receipt for goods shipped, evidence of the contract of carriage and a document of title that allows the goods to be transferred by endorsement. Stating the country of manufacture is the job of a certificate of origin. Options C, D and B are all genuine functions of a bill of lading.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Which shipping document gives its holder the right to take delivery of the goods and can be transferred by endorsement, making it a document of title?

options.a: Insurance certificate
options.b: Certificate of origin

questions.explanation: The bill of lading is a document of title, so whoever lawfully holds it can claim the goods, which is why banks keep it until the buyer pays or accepts. Option D shows the price and description of the goods, option B states where they were made, and option A proves that the goods are insured; none of them gives control over the goods.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A certificate of origin presented with export documents serves mainly to

options.a: evidence the contract between the exporter and the shipping line
options.b: prove that the goods are covered against loss in transit
options.c: state the country in which the goods were produced or manufactured
options.d: show the price, quantity and description of the goods sold

questions.explanation: A certificate of origin confirms where the goods were made, which matters for customs duties, trade agreements and import rules. Option A is a function of the bill of lading, option D is the role of the commercial invoice, and option B is the role of the insurance certificate or policy.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: The shipping document prepared by the seller that shows the description, quantity, unit price and total value of the goods, and is used for payment and customs valuation, is the

options.a: bill of lading
options.b: certificate of origin

questions.explanation: The commercial invoice is the seller's bill to the buyer, setting out what was sold and for how much. Option A is issued by the carrier as a receipt and document of title, option B states the country of manufacture, and option D covers the goods against loss or damage in transit.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Goods shipped from Apapa on CIF terms are damaged by sea water during the voyage. To claim compensation, the buyer will rely mainly on the

options.a: certificate of origin
options.b: commercial invoice

questions.explanation: The insurance policy or certificate is evidence that the goods are covered against loss or damage in transit, and it is the basis of any claim against the insurer. Option A only states where the goods were made, and option B shows their price and description. Option C is a Nigerian export proceeds form, not an insurance document.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Mr Okonkwo, a Lagos trader, wants to import machinery from China through his bank. Under Nigerian import procedures, the statutory document he must first complete and register electronically through his authorised dealer bank, supported by a proforma invoice, is

options.a: Form M
options.b: Form NXP

questions.explanation: Form M is the statutory document required for physical imports into Nigeria, processed electronically through an authorised dealer bank and supported by a proforma invoice and other documents. Option B is for export proceeds, and option C is used for invisible transactions such as school fees and travel, not imports of goods. Option D is issued by the shipping company after goods are shipped.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: In Nigeria, the statutory form completed by an exporter through his bank so that the export and the repatriation of its proceeds can be documented and tracked is the

options.a: Form NXP (Nigerian Export Proceeds Form)
options.b: Certificate of Origin

questions.explanation: Form NXP, the Nigerian Export Proceeds Form, is completed through the exporter's bank to document an export and the proceeds that must come back to Nigeria. Option C is the import counterpart, used before goods are brought in. Option D relates to invisible payments, and option B only states where the goods were made.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A domiciliary account in a Nigerian bank is

options.a: an account a Nigerian bank keeps with a correspondent bank abroad
options.b: an account a foreign bank keeps with a Nigerian bank in naira
options.c: an account held in a foreign currency, such as US dollars, in a bank in Nigeria
options.d: a naira account opened only for customers who live near the branch

questions.explanation: A domiciliary account lets a customer hold, receive and pay out foreign currency through a bank in Nigeria, which is useful for exporters receiving dollar proceeds and importers making foreign payments. Option A is a nostro account and option B is a vostro account, both kept between banks. Option D confuses 'domiciliary' with where the customer lives.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: The key difference between a spot foreign exchange transaction and a forward foreign exchange contract is that

options.a: a spot deal is used only by banks, while a forward contract is used only by importers
options.b: a spot deal involves two currencies, while a forward contract involves only one
options.c: a spot deal fixes a rate for a future date, while a forward contract is settled immediately
options.d: a spot deal is settled almost immediately at today's rate, while a forward contract fixes a rate today for exchange at a future date

questions.explanation: A spot transaction is settled within a very short period, normally two business days, at the current rate, whereas a forward contract locks in an agreed rate now for delivery of the currency later. Option B reverses the two. Options A and C are not real distinctions, since both deals are used by many market participants and both always involve two currencies.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A Lagos importer must pay a US supplier $40,000 in three months' time and fears the naira may weaken before then. To remove this exchange rate risk, his bank can best offer him

options.a: a clean collection
options.b: a spot purchase of dollars in three months' time

questions.explanation: A forward contract fixes today the rate at which the importer will buy dollars in three months, so a later fall in the naira will not raise his naira cost. Option B leaves him fully exposed, because he would buy at whatever rate prevails then. Option A is a way of collecting payment, and option C is a domestic payment instruction; neither manages exchange risk.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: An importer books a forward contract with his bank to buy $25,000 in three months at N1,520 per dollar. On the settlement date the spot rate is N1,560 per dollar. How much naira does the forward contract save him compared with buying at the spot rate on that day?
questions.explanation: At spot he would pay $25,000 x N1,560 = N39,000,000, but under the forward contract he pays $25,000 x N1,520 = N38,000,000, saving N1,000,000. Options B and D are the total costs under each rate rather than the saving. Option C is just the rate difference of N40 multiplied by 1,000 instead of by 25,000.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A bank finances a Sapele timber exporter to buy, process and pack the timber before it is shipped, and later discounts the export bill after shipment. These two facilities are, respectively,

options.a: factoring and forfaiting
options.b: pre-shipment finance and post-shipment finance
options.d: import finance and export credit insurance

questions.explanation: Pre-shipment (packing) finance helps the exporter produce or buy the goods before shipping, while post-shipment finance, such as negotiating or discounting the export bill, bridges the gap between shipment and receipt of the proceeds. Option C reverses the order. Option D is wrong because both facilities are export finance, and option A names other specialised receivables techniques.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: The Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM) was established by

options.a: the Central Bank of Nigeria Act of 1958, as a department of the CBN
options.b: the NEXIM Act No. 38 of 1991, owned jointly by the Federal Government and the Central Bank of Nigeria
options.c: a 2001 CBN circular introducing universal banking
options.d: the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act of 1991, as a commercial bank

questions.explanation: NEXIM was set up by the Nigerian Export-Import Bank Act No. 38 of 1991 as Nigeria's export credit agency, with its capital subscribed equally by the Federal Government and the CBN. Option D is the general banking law, not NEXIM's establishing Act. Options A and C refer to the central bank's own statute and to the universal banking era, which have nothing to do with NEXIM's creation.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM)?

options.a: Maintaining a foreign exchange revolving fund lent to exporters to import inputs
options.b: Providing investment guarantee and investment insurance facilities to exporters
options.c: Providing export credit guarantee and credit insurance facilities to Nigerian exporters
options.d: Granting long-term mortgage loans to individuals for home ownership

questions.explanation: NEXIM is an export credit agency, so its work centres on export guarantees, credit insurance, a foreign exchange revolving fund and investment guarantees for exporters. Housing finance is the business of mortgage institutions such as the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria. Options C, A and B are all listed NEXIM functions.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: A Nigerian exporter of processed cashew fears that his buyer in another country may fail to pay because of war or a ban on foreign currency transfers in that country. The facility that protects him against both such political risks and the buyer's commercial default is

options.a: a domiciliary account in Nigeria
options.b: export credit insurance, such as that offered by NEXIM
options.c: a clean collection through his bank
options.d: a nostro account with a foreign bank

questions.explanation: Export credit insurance compensates the exporter when a foreign buyer fails to pay for commercial reasons (such as insolvency) or political reasons (such as war or transfer restrictions); NEXIM provides this cover for Nigerian exporters. Options D and A are simply accounts for holding currency and offer no protection against default. Option C is a payment method in which the bank gives no guarantee at all.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: In the operation of the Nigerian Export-Import Bank, the foreign exchange revolving fund is meant to

options.a: settle the clearing balances of deposit money banks
options.b: lend foreign exchange to exporters to import inputs needed to produce exportable goods
options.c: finance government imports of petroleum products
options.d: pay school fees and medical bills of Nigerians abroad

questions.explanation: NEXIM maintains a foreign exchange revolving fund from which exporters borrow to import raw inputs and other items used in producing goods for export. Option D describes invisible personal payments, and option C is not an export promotion activity. Option A relates to the clearing system, which is outside NEXIM's role.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes forfaiting from factoring?

options.a: Forfaiting is the purchase, without recourse, of medium-term export receivables such as avalised bills, while factoring is the sale of short-term book debts
options.b: Forfaiting is a type of letter of credit, while factoring is a type of documentary collection
options.c: Forfaiting is lending against landed property, while factoring is lending against shares
options.d: Forfaiting is the sale of short-term book debts, while factoring buys medium-term export bills without recourse

questions.explanation: Factoring is essentially the sale of book debts, usually short-term trade receivables, whereas forfaiting is the without-recourse purchase of medium-term export receivables, typically bills of exchange or similar negotiable instruments guaranteed (avalised) by a bank. Option D swaps the two. Options B and C confuse them with payment methods and with secured lending.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: In providing foreign exchange services under correspondent banking, Nigerian merchant banks

options.a: participate directly in the cheque clearing house
options.b: accept savings deposits from individual customers with passbooks
options.c: arrange the confirmation of letters of credit for their clients
options.d: issue travellers cheques to retail customers in rural branches

questions.explanation: Merchant banks provide foreign exchange services to corporate clients on a wholesale basis, and under correspondent banking they arrange for clients' letters of credit to be confirmed. Option A is wrong because merchant banks are not members of the clearing house. Options D and B are retail services more typical of commercial banks.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: The traditional first function of merchant banks, in which they add their name to bills of exchange to finance the trade of others, is

options.a: equipment leasing
options.b: acceptance

questions.explanation: Acceptance is the classic merchant banking function: the bank accepts bills of exchange so that its customers' trade can be financed on the strength of the bank's name. Option A involves hiring out assets, option D funds large new projects through a special entity, and option C helps companies raise capital from the public.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a role of commercial banks in international trade?

options.a: Discounting documentary credits so that sellers are paid at once
options.b: Fixing the official exchange rate of the naira
options.c: Acting as referees on the creditworthiness of exporters
options.d: Confirming letters of credit to reduce default in payment

questions.explanation: Commercial banks help foreign trade by providing documentary credits, discounting them, confirming letters of credit, acting as referees and dealing in foreign exchange. Managing the exchange rate is a monetary authority matter for the Central Bank of Nigeria, not a service a commercial bank sells to traders. Options A, C and D are all genuine roles.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Before signing a large supply contract, a Ghanaian importer asks for information on the financial standing of a Nigerian exporter. The exporter's bank provides a confidential reply on his creditworthiness. In this role the bank is

options.a: operating a vostro account for the importer
options.b: acting as a referee by giving a status opinion
options.d: acting as an issuing bank under a letter of credit

questions.explanation: Banks act as referees for their customers by giving status opinions or bankers' references on creditworthiness, usually in general and confidential terms. Option D involves opening a credit, not reporting on a customer, and option C involves lending to the exporter after shipment. Option A is a correspondent account between banks.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: When a Nigerian bank actually remits payment abroad for a customer's international transaction, which of the following channels is commonly used?

options.a: Standing order card
options.b: Intra-bank transfer between the customer's own accounts

questions.explanation: In international payments the actual remittance is made by mail transfer, telegraphic transfer or bank draft, with telegraphic or wire transfer being the fast option. Options A and C are domestic methods for regular or creditor-initiated payments. Option B only moves money between the same customer's accounts within one bank.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Why do exporters generally prefer documentary collection to open account, even though neither gives a bank guarantee of payment?

options.a: Because a collection is cheaper than open account, which carries high bank charges
options.b: Because a collection allows the exporter to receive payment before shipping the goods
options.c: Because in a collection the shipping documents stay under bank control until the buyer pays or accepts the bill
options.d: Because in a collection the importer's bank must pay even if the importer refuses

questions.explanation: In a documentary collection the exporter's bank and the collecting bank hold the documents of title and release them only against payment or acceptance, so the buyer cannot simply take the goods without paying or accepting. Option D describes a letter of credit, not a collection. Option B describes advance payment, and option A is not the reason, since open account involves the least bank handling.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Under a documentary credit, if the documents presented by the exporter do NOT match the terms of the credit, the issuing bank

options.a: must still pay, since it has already issued an irrevocable credit
options.b: must inspect the goods to decide whether to pay
options.c: is entitled to refuse payment because the presentation is not complying
options.d: must pay half and hold the rest until the importer agrees

questions.explanation: The bank's undertaking is to pay against a complying presentation, so documents with discrepancies give it the right to refuse, although it may approach the applicant for a waiver. Option A ignores the condition that documents must comply. Options B and D are wrong because banks deal in documents, not goods, and there is no rule of part payment.

questions.topic: Bank Account Services for Exporters and Importers
questions.question: Unlike a bill of lading, an air waybill used for goods sent by air from Lagos

options.a: states the country in which the goods were made
options.b: must be endorsed to transfer ownership of the goods
options.c: is issued by the exporter rather than the carrier
options.d: is not a document of title, so the goods can be released to the named consignee without it

questions.explanation: An air waybill is a receipt and evidence of the contract of carriage, but it is not a document of title; the airline delivers the goods to the named consignee. Option B describes a negotiable bill of lading, which is a document of title. Option C is wrong because the carrier or its agent issues it, and option A is the job of a certificate of origin.

questions.question: When a lending banker carries out a status enquiry into a prospective borrower's background and integrity, which of the 5 Cs of lending is being assessed?

options.a: Collateral
options.b: Conditions

questions.explanation: Character concerns the borrower's honesty, reputation and willingness to repay, and banks check it through background or status enquiries before granting a loan. Option C looks at how much of the borrower's own money is committed to the business, option A is the security the bank can fall back on if the loan is not repaid, and option B refers to the state of the economy and other external circumstances.

questions.question: In bank lending, collateral (security) mainly serves to

options.a: replace the need to assess the borrower's ability to repay
options.b: give the bank something to fall back on if the borrower fails to repay
options.c: prove that the borrower has the legal capacity to contract
options.d: fix the interest rate on the loan

questions.explanation: Collateral is a safeguard: if the borrower defaults, the bank can realise the security to recover what it is owed. Option A is a common misconception, because sound lending still depends mainly on the borrower's ability and willingness to repay, with security only as a fallback. Option C relates to capacity, not security, and option D is wrong because security does not by itself determine the interest rate.

questions.question: An arrangement under which a current account holder is allowed to withdraw more than the balance in the account, up to an agreed limit, is called:

options.a: A term loan
options.b: A standing order

questions.explanation: An overdraft lets a current account customer draw beyond the credit balance up to an agreed limit, and interest is charged only on the amount actually overdrawn; businesses often use it to smooth out working capital needs. Option A is a fixed sum lent for a set period and repaid by instalments, while option D means the bank buys a bill before it matures for less than its face value. Option B is simply an instruction to the bank to make regular payments from the account.

questions.question: In bank lending, the difference between the market value of the security offered by a borrower and the amount of the loan granted against it is called the:

options.a: Equity of redemption
options.b: Interest spread

questions.explanation: The margin is the cushion a banker keeps by lending less than the security is worth, so that a fall in its value or the cost of selling it will not leave the bank exposed. Option A is a mortgagor's right to recover the mortgaged property once the debt is repaid. Option B is the gap between lending and deposit interest rates, and option C is a promise by a third party to pay if the borrower defaults, not a difference in values.

questions.question: Mr Eze was granted a vehicle loan of N200,000.00 on 1 January 1996, repayable over 2 years in 4 equal semi-annual instalments, with interest at 10% per annum calculated on a simple (flat) basis on the original principal. The loan was credited to his current account, which already had a credit balance of N40,000.00, and each repayment of principal and interest is debited to that account. How much is debited to his current account on each half-yearly repayment date?
questions.explanation: Total flat interest is P x R x T = N200,000 x 0.10 x 2 = N40,000, or N10,000 for each of the 4 half-years, while each principal instalment is N200,000 / 4 = N50,000. Each repayment date therefore carries N50,000 + N10,000 = N60,000, which takes the account from N240,000 CR down to nil after the fourth payment. Option C leaves out the interest, option A charges a full year's interest (N20,000) every half-year, and option D calculates interest only on the instalment rather than on the original principal.

questions.question: A lending banker refuses to finance a customer's gambling business even though the customer offers good security. Which principle of lending is the banker applying?

options.a: Profitability
options.b: Suitability

questions.explanation: Suitability asks whether the purpose of an advance is acceptable; banks should not finance gambling, betting or other speculative activities or anything against government policy, however good the security. Option A concerns earning a return, option C concerns how quickly the funds come back, and option D is already covered here by the good security.

questions.question: Which of the following is often described as the real security for any bank advance?

options.a: A legal mortgage over landed property
options.b: The character of the borrower
options.c: A guarantee from a third party
options.d: Shares quoted on the stock exchange

questions.explanation: A good lending proposal should stand on its own, and the borrower's integrity, honesty and reliability are what really ensure repayment. Options A, C and D are acceptable forms of collateral, but they only protect the bank if things go wrong.

questions.question: In banking, the extension of a credit facility to an intending borrower on the understanding that the principal and the interest on it will be repaid at an agreed future date is called

options.a: Borrowing
options.b: Financial disintermediation

questions.explanation: Bank lending is the bank's act of extending credit to a borrower, who must repay the principal plus interest at an agreed future date. Option A describes the same transaction from the customer's side, the ability to obtain credit, not the bank's act of granting it. Options D and B concern gathering deposits and bypassing banks, not granting credit.

questions.question: The ability of a willing and creditworthy customer to obtain a credit facility from a bank or other loan provider, with a view to repaying the sum at an agreed future date, is best described as

options.a: Borrowing
options.b: Discounting

questions.explanation: Borrowing is the customer's side of a credit transaction: a willing, creditworthy person obtains funds and undertakes to repay them later. Option C is the bank's act of extending the credit, while B is buying a bill before maturity and D is promising to answer for another person's debt.

questions.question: Lending bankers usually charge a higher rate of interest on a facility mainly in order to

options.a: raise the bank's cash reserve ratio with the CBN
options.b: reduce the amount of security the borrower must provide
options.c: guarantee that depositors can withdraw at any time
options.d: compensate the bank for the risk that the borrower may default

questions.explanation: Every loan carries a risk that the principal or interest will not be repaid, so the interest charged includes compensation for that risk of default. Option A is a CBN reserve requirement and has nothing to do with the rate charged to a borrower. Option B is wrong because a higher rate does not replace security, and C is about the bank's liquidity, not loan pricing.

questions.question: In bank lending, interest is best described as

options.a: the difference between the market value of a security and the loan granted
options.b: the value of the asset pledged by the borrower as security for the loan
options.c: the portion of the loan that is repaid at the end of each period
options.d: the return paid by the borrower to the provider of funds, usually stated as a percentage of the principal

questions.explanation: Interest is the reward the borrower pays the lender for the use of the funds, normally quoted as a percentage of the principal per month or per annum. Option B describes security or collateral, C describes a principal instalment, and A describes the margin on a security.

questions.question: A loan or advance granted by a bank is described as a risk asset because

options.a: it is held as cash in the bank's vault
options.b: it must be backed by treasury bills
options.c: the recovery of all the credit extended to the customer is uncertain
options.d: it carries no interest until it is repaid

questions.explanation: Loans are called risk assets because the bank cannot be sure of recovering every naira lent, so the possibility of loss always exists. Option A describes cash, the most liquid asset, which is not a loan. Options B and D are not features of loans: advances need not be backed by treasury bills, and they earn interest while outstanding.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the five Cs of bank lending?

options.a: Character
options.b: Currency

questions.explanation: The five Cs of bank lending are character, capacity, capital, collateral and condition, so currency is the odd one out. Options A, C and D are all genuine members of the five Cs.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the five Cs of bank lending?

options.a: Clearing
options.b: Capacity

questions.explanation: Capacity is one of the five Cs, alongside character, capital, collateral and condition. Option A is the process of settling cheques between banks, C is a charge for a banking service and D is a group of lenders sharing a large loan, none of which is one of the five Cs.

questions.question: Among the five Cs of lending, the one regarded as the first and the best security a borrower can offer a bank is

options.a: Capital
options.b: Collateral

questions.explanation: A borrower's character, meaning his integrity, reliability and past record with money, is regarded as the first and best security because an honest borrower repays willingly. Option B is the tempting answer, but collateral is treated as the last and least consideration, only a fallback. Options A and D concern the owner's stake and the state of the economy.

questions.question: Which of the five Cs of lending is described as the last and least consideration, a residual matter that is not crucial to the final lending decision?

options.a: Collateral
options.b: Character

questions.explanation: Collateral is only a cushion the bank falls back on if the borrower defaults, so it is the last and least factor in the decision to lend. Option B is the opposite, being the first and best security, while D and C are examined before the bank looks at the security.

questions.question: During an economic recession, a Lagos bank decides to cut back new loans to hotels and event centres even for customers with good records. The C of lending the bank is applying here is

options.a: Condition
options.b: Collateral

questions.explanation: Condition refers to the state of the economy and the business environment, such as a recession or high inflation, which can affect a borrower's ability to repay. Option D concerns the borrower's personal integrity, which is not in doubt here. Options C and B relate to the owner's stake and the security offered, not to the economic climate.

questions.question: Before approving a N50 million loan for a cassava processing plant, a bank insists that the promoters must first put a substantial sum of their own money into the project. The bank is assessing the borrower's

options.a: Condition
options.b: Capital

questions.explanation: Capital is the owners' own contribution to the project, and banks want it to be substantial so that the borrower has a real stake in success. Option C is about integrity and track record, A is about the economic environment, and D is about the asset pledged as a fallback.

questions.question: Lending bankers insist that a borrower contributes a reasonable proportion of a project's finance mainly because

options.a: the borrower's contribution replaces the need for a status enquiry
options.b: the contribution makes the bank a shareholder in the borrower's business
options.c: a borrower with little of his own money at stake may not be committed, leaving the risk of failure mostly on the bank
options.d: the bank is not allowed to finance more than one stage of a project

questions.explanation: When the bank finances almost everything, the borrower has little to lose and may not work hard to make the project succeed, so the risk falls mainly on the bank; the higher his own investment, the greater his determination. Option A is wrong because capital does not replace checking character, and B is wrong because a lender does not become an owner. Option D invents a rule that does not exist.

questions.question: A bank may sometimes grant an advance without demanding collateral. This is most likely where the borrower

options.a: is a minor whose parents own the business
options.b: is highly creditworthy with a proven good track record
options.c: refuses to disclose the purpose of the loan
options.d: intends to use the funds for sports betting

questions.explanation: Because collateral is only a fallback, a bank can lend unsecured to a highly creditworthy customer with a good record. Option A is wrong because a minor cannot validly contract with a bank, D is a speculative purpose banks avoid, and C fails the basic check on purpose, so none of these would attract even a secured loan.

questions.question: The process by which a lending banker obtains background information on a prospective borrower, to find out whether he is prudent or prodigal with borrowed funds, is known as

options.a: Land registry search
options.b: Status enquiry

questions.explanation: A status enquiry is the banker's investigation of a customer's background, integrity and conduct with money, often through references and reports from other banks. Option A is a search to verify title to land offered as security, C is the sharing of a large loan among several lenders, and D is matching account records.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the objectives banks seek to achieve when granting credit facilities?

options.a: Speculation
options.b: Suitability

questions.explanation: The objectives of bank lending are growth, profitability, safety, liquidity and suitability; speculation is something banks avoid when lending. Options D, C and B are genuine objectives of bank lending.

questions.question: The ability of a bank's loans, advances and investments to yield good returns to its shareholders is the lending objective of

options.a: Profitability
options.b: Liquidity

questions.explanation: Profitability is about loans and investments earning good returns so that shareholders' funds are worthwhile. Option B is about having cash available for withdrawals, C is about protecting depositors' funds, and D is about loans contributing to the progress of the bank and the economy.

questions.question: The ease with which a bank's assets can be quickly converted into cash to meet depositors' withdrawals and the requirements of the CBN describes the lending objective of

options.a: Safety
options.b: Suitability

questions.explanation: Liquidity is the availability of money, or the ease of turning assets into cash to meet withdrawals, new loan requests and CBN requirements.
