Option D is about earning returns, B is about loans fitting the bank's policy and regulations, and A is about protecting depositors' funds rather than having cash on hand.

questions.question: The lending objective which requires that a bank should not commit all its loans to long-term projects, and that its lending must comply with the rules of the regulatory authorities, is

options.a: Liquidity
options.b: Growth

questions.explanation: Suitability means loans must fit the bank's policy, the length of repayment period it can bear and the regulators' rules. Option B relates to the contribution of lending to progress, C to returns, and A to cash availability; liquidity is affected by long-term lending, but the objective stated here, covering bank policy and regulation, is suitability.

questions.question: The lending objective concerned with safeguarding depositors' funds so that depositors can withdraw their money on demand without delay is

options.a: Suitability
options.b: Growth

questions.explanation: Safety is about protecting depositors' funds and the loans granted, so that the public keeps confidence in the bank. Option C focuses on returns to shareholders, B on the contribution of loans to progress, and A on matching loans to the bank's policy and regulations.

questions.question: If a bank granted almost all of its deposits as loans and kept very little cash, the lending objective it would most directly fail to meet is

options.a: Liquidity
options.b: Growth

questions.explanation: Lending out nearly all deposits leaves the bank unable to meet depositors' withdrawals and the CBN's liquidity requirements, which is a failure of liquidity. Option D would actually tend to rise in the short run because more funds earn interest. Options B and C are not the objective most directly hurt by running out of cash.

questions.question: A bank that kept all its deposits in the form of physical cash, granting no loans at all, would mainly sacrifice

options.a: Safety
options.b: Profitability

questions.explanation: Cash earns nothing, so a bank that holds all deposits as cash gives up the interest it would earn on loans and becomes unprofitable. Option D would be at its highest in this case, not sacrificed. Option A is not the main loss, and C is a quality of a security rather than a lending objective.

questions.question: In the classic three-principle view of bank lending (safety, suitability and profitability), which principle is described as being of paramount importance to the bank?

options.a: Suitability
options.b: Safety

questions.explanation: Safety is treated as paramount because the funds lent are mainly depositors' money, so the bank must be sure of the borrower's integrity and of where the repayment will come from. Options A and C are the other two principles but are not described as paramount, and D is not one of the three principles in this formulation.

questions.question: A customer with a strong repayment record asks his bank for a loan to stake on football betting. The bank declines because the purpose conflicts with sound lending policy. The lending principle applied is

options.a: Capital
options.b: Liquidity

questions.explanation: Suitability requires that the purpose of an advance be acceptable and not conflict with government policy, and bankers are not expected to finance gambling, betting or other speculative activities. Option C could even favour the loan if the rate were high, B concerns the bank's cash position, and A is the borrower's own contribution.

questions.question: When a lending officer asks a loan applicant 'What is the source of repayment?', the canon of lending being examined is

options.a: Amount
options.b: Purpose

questions.explanation: Asking how and from what funds the loan will be paid back tests the repayment plan, which must be convincing before a bank lends. Option A asks how much is needed, D asks for how long, and B asks what the money is for.

questions.question: A bank that lends a customer less than his project genuinely needs runs the risk that

options.a: the customer will repay the loan too early
options.b: the bank's liquidity ratio will become too high
options.c: the project may be abandoned uncompleted, so that repayment does not come
options.d: the security will automatically be released to the customer

questions.explanation: Underestimating a borrower's needs can force awkward 'topping up' decisions later or leave the project abandoned, in which case the loan may not be repaid. Option A is not a danger of lending too little, B confuses one small loan with the bank's overall ratios, and D has no basis because security is released only when the loan is repaid.

questions.question: Adekunle Plastics Ltd wants a short-term facility repayable within months to pay for a new factory building. A lending banker would be concerned mainly because

options.a: the firm would be borrowing short and investing long in fixed assets that are not quickly saleable
options.b: a factory building is a current asset of the business
options.c: short-term facilities do not attract any interest
options.d: fixed assets can never be used as security for a bank loan

questions.explanation: Using short-term borrowing to buy fixed assets makes the firm 'borrow short and invest long'; since fixed assets cannot be sold quickly at a good price, the firm's financial position becomes riskier. Option D is false because land and buildings are common securities, C is false because short-term facilities do carry interest, and B is wrong because a building is a fixed asset.

questions.question: Nigerian commercial banks have traditionally preferred to grant short-term working capital finance rather than medium or long-term loans mainly because

options.a: most of their deposits are short-term in nature
options.b: the CBN forbids them from lending for more than one year
options.c: short-term loans never require any security
options.d: long-term loans cannot earn any interest

questions.explanation: Since bank deposits are commonly short-term and withdrawable, banks prefer short-term working capital lending and often refer medium-term requests to merchant banks and development institutions such as the Bank of Industry. Option B overstates the position because there is no outright ban, C is false because short-term loans may be secured, and D is false because long-term loans do earn interest.

questions.question: To judge whether a company's proposed repayment plan is feasible, a lending banker would normally ask the company for

options.a: its certificate of occupancy and a survey plan only
options.b: a list of its staff and their dates of employment
options.c: its share register and the minutes of its last annual general meeting
options.d: a cash budget, a projected profit and loss account and a projected balance sheet

questions.explanation: A business repays from future profits and cash flows, so the banker needs forward-looking statements such as a cash budget, projected profit and loss account and projected balance sheet. Options C and B show ownership and staffing, not ability to repay. Option A relates to land offered as security, which is a fallback rather than proof of repayment capacity.

questions.question: In loan appraisal, examining a firm's balance sheets and profit and loss accounts for about three years to see whether it can remain a going concern if its plans suffer a setback tests the

options.a: duration of the loan
options.b: strength of the business

questions.explanation: Strength of the business asks whether the firm is financially strong enough to keep going if things go wrong, which is judged by analysing several years of accounts. Option D looks at what the money is for, A at how long it is needed and C at how much is needed.

questions.question: Which of the following loan purposes would a lending banker in Nigeria be LEAST willing to finance?

options.a: An activity that is illegal under Nigerian law
options.b: Purchase of raw materials by a bakery
options.d: Working capital for a licensed pharmacy

questions.explanation: The purpose of a loan must be legal and within the CBN's regulatory lending framework, because the law punishes parties to illegal contracts. Options D, B and C are ordinary working capital needs of legitimate businesses, the kind of short-term lending banks favour.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the basic questions a lending officer should ask on receiving a loan request?

options.a: For how long is the money needed?
options.b: What security can the customer offer?
options.c: How many branches does the customer's bank have?
options.d: How much does the customer require?

questions.explanation: The canons of lending ask how much, why, for how long, where repayment will come from, how strong the business is, what security is offered and what the customer is like. The number of branches a bank has is irrelevant to the borrower's creditworthiness. Options D, A and B are genuine canon questions.

questions.question: An asset that a bank accepts from a borrower for a loan facility, to protect the bank should the borrower fail to honour his obligation, is called

options.a: Security
options.b: Margin

questions.explanation: Security, or collateral, is the asset a lender holds as protection in case the borrower defaults, much like insurance against the unexpected. Option B is the excess of the security's value over the loan, C is the price of the loan, and D is a period during which no repayment is required.

questions.question: An enforceable legal claim on collateral that has been pledged to obtain a loan, giving the lender the right to repossess the property if the borrower fails to repay, is known as a

options.a: security interest
options.b: equity of redemption

questions.explanation: A security interest is the lender's enforceable legal claim over pledged assets, allowing repossession on default. Option B is the borrower's right to recover mortgaged property on paying off the debt, D is a repayment holiday, and C is the document setting out the terms of a facility.

questions.question: Under Nigeria's Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act, a manager or other officer of a bank may grant an advance, loan or credit facility to a person only if

options.a: the facility has first been approved by the NDIC
options.b: it is authorised in accordance with the rules and regulations of the bank
options.c: the borrower is related to a director of the bank
options.d: the borrower has kept an account with the bank for at least five years

questions.explanation: The Act forbids bank officers from granting any advance, loan or credit facility unless it is authorised under the bank's own rules and regulations, including its rules on security. Option D invents a time requirement, A wrongly gives the deposit insurer an approval role, and C describes insider lending, which raises concern rather than providing authority.

questions.question: Where security is required for an advance, sound lending practice is that the bank should

options.a: allow the borrower to keep the title documents until the final instalment
options.b: take security only for loans to companies and never for individuals
options.c: disburse the funds first and take security only if the borrower defaults
options.d: obtain and perfect the security before disbursing the funds

questions.explanation: A banker must ensure that security is properly taken and perfected before any money is released, otherwise there may be nothing enforceable to fall back on. Option C reverses the correct order, A leaves the bank without control of the title, and B is false because individuals routinely provide securities such as land, shares and life policies.

questions.question: One reason banks demand security for credit facilities is that a customer who has deposited his property or title documents with the bank is more likely to

options.a: avoid providing financial statements to the bank
options.b: withdraw his deposits from the bank quickly
options.c: demand a lower rate of interest than other borrowers
options.d: use the funds judiciously for the purpose for which they were granted

questions.explanation: Having his property at stake makes a borrower careful to use the money well on the agreed project, which is one of the reasons for demanding security. Options C, B and A are not results of giving security and do not explain why banks ask for it.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a quality of a good banking security?

options.a: High maintenance cost
options.b: Undoubted title

questions.explanation: A good security should be cheap to take and hold, so a high maintenance cost is a drawback rather than a quality. Options C, D and B are all genuine qualities: a ready market, a stable price and certain ownership.

questions.question: Mrs Bello offers her shop as security, but a search shows it is already charged to another bank for an earlier loan. The quality of good security that the shop lacks is

options.a: Stability of value
options.b: Marketability

questions.explanation: Non-encumbrance means the asset is free from prior charges and third-party claims; if it is already charged to another lender, the new bank would have only a secondary claim. Options B, A and D may all be satisfied by the shop, since it can be saleable, stable and rent-yielding while still carrying a prior charge.

questions.question: Bankers are generally reluctant to accept luxury goods as security, compared with necessities, mainly because luxury goods

options.a: can never be insured against loss
options.b: are always encumbered by prior charges
options.c: have prices that fluctuate widely with changes in fashion and taste
options.d: cannot legally be owned by individuals in Nigeria

questions.explanation: A good security should be stable in value; luxury goods swing widely in price as fashions and tastes change, whereas necessities are more stable in the short run. Options D, A and B are untrue generalisations about luxury goods.

questions.question: The quality of a good security which requires that it has a ready, broad market so the bank can sell it to recover the loan is

options.a: Non-encumbrance
options.b: Marketability

questions.explanation: Marketability means the security can easily find buyers, because the bank takes it not to keep it but to sell it if the borrower defaults. Option D is about the value covering the loan, C is about the asset being lawful to own, and A is about it being free from prior charges.

questions.question: The requirement that the value of a security must be enough to cover the full amount of the loan, with a reasonable margin over it, is the quality of

options.a: Liquidity
options.b: Marketability

questions.explanation: Adequacy means the security's value fully covers the bank's exposure and leaves a margin, so that a fall in value or costs of sale still leave the loan covered. Option A is about how quickly the asset turns into cash, B about having a ready market, and D about properly executed deeds and agreements.

questions.question: Two plots are offered to a bank as security: a vacant plot, and a block of flats let out to tenants who pay rent throughout the loan period. Other things being equal, the bank prefers the block of flats because of the security quality of

options.a: Undoubted title
options.b: Non-encumbrance

questions.explanation: An asset that generates earnings while the loan is outstanding is a better security than one that does not, which is why rented flats are preferred. Options B, D and A could be equally satisfied by both plots, so they do not explain the preference.

questions.question: Mr Ojo offers his late father's house as security, but the property has not been transferred into his name and other family members dispute his claim to it. The quality of good security most clearly missing is

options.a: Undoubted title (ownership)
options.b: Stability of value

questions.explanation: A good security must belong to the borrower beyond doubt, because a defective or disputed title can leave the bank unable to enforce or sell it. Options B, D and C relate to price, ease of sale and earnings, none of which cures a disputed ownership.

questions.question: A bank should not accept as security an asset that is illegal to own or possess mainly because

options.a: the bank would face difficulty disposing of it and could face legal consequences
options.b: illegal assets cannot be valued by an estate surveyor
options.c: illegal assets always fall in value quickly
options.d: the borrower would be unable to pay interest on the loan

questions.explanation: Legal acceptability is a quality of good security: an asset that is unlawful to possess cannot be sold openly when the borrower defaults, and holding it may expose the bank itself to legal action. Options C, B and D do not state the real problem, which is unenforceability and legal risk.

questions.question: Which of the following is a personal security?

options.a: A pledge of goods in a warehouse
options.b: A guarantee given by a third party
options.d: A fixed charge over a machine

questions.explanation: Personal security is a promise by a person, such as a guarantee, rather than a charge over a specific tangible asset. Options C, A and D are non-personal securities because each gives the bank rights over identifiable property.

questions.question: Non-personal (tangible) security is generally regarded as safer for a bank than personal security because

options.a: it is always more liquid than a cash deposit
options.b: a tangible property can be sold in the market to recover the unpaid amount if the borrower defaults
options.c: it removes the need to assess the borrower's character
options.d: it never needs to be valued before the loan is granted

questions.explanation: With tangible property the bank can realise the asset and recover what is owed, whereas a personal guarantee depends on the guarantor's willingness and means to pay. Option D is false because tangible securities must be valued, C is false because character remains the first consideration, and A is false because nothing is more liquid than cash.

questions.question: Compared with freehold land, leasehold land offered as security has the disadvantage that

options.a: its value falls as the unexpired years of the lease reduce
options.b: it lasts indefinitely and cannot be sold
options.c: it can never be mortgaged to a bank
options.d: it gives the holder absolute title to the land

questions.explanation: A leasehold title runs only until the lease expires, after which possession reverts to the freeholder, so its value shrinks as the remaining term gets shorter. Option C is false since leaseholds are commonly mortgaged, while B and D describe freehold rather than leasehold.

questions.question: A form of security created by contract which gives a lender an interest in a borrower's property until a given sum of money is repaid, usually created by a written agreement registered at the land registry, is a

options.a: Hypothecation
options.b: Lien

questions.explanation: A mortgage gives the lender an interest in property, usually land and buildings, as security for repayment, and it is created by a written agreement registered with the land authority. Option B is a right to retain goods already in the creditor's possession, A is a charge over goods that stay with the borrower, and C is a promise by a third party.

questions.question: Mr Adewale deposits the title deeds of his house with his bank as security, but the legal estate is not transferred to the bank and he continues to live in the house. This arrangement is

options.a: a legal mortgage
options.b: a pledge

questions.explanation: In an equitable mortgage the lender holds the title deeds while the property remains with the mortgagor, and no legal estate passes to the lender. Option A would require a deed transferring legal title to the bank, B applies to movable goods delivered to the lender, and C is a promise by a third party.

questions.question: The essential feature of a legal mortgage is that it

options.a: gives the lender possession of movable goods only
options.b: vests a legal estate in the mortgagee and must be created by a mortgage deed
options.c: is an oral promise by a third party to pay the debt
options.d: leaves the legal estate with the borrower and is created by depositing title deeds

questions.explanation: A legal mortgage transfers legal title in the property to the lender, together with a right of possession, and must be executed under seal as a mortgage deed. Option D describes an equitable mortgage, A describes a pledge and C describes a guarantee, which in any case is normally in writing.

questions.question: In a mortgage transaction where a bank lends to a customer on the security of his house, the customer and the bank are respectively called the

options.a: mortgagee and the mortgagor
options.b: mortgagor and the mortgagee

questions.explanation: The borrower who gives the mortgage over his property is the mortgagor, and the lender who receives it is the mortgagee. Option A reverses the two terms, C names parties to a guarantee, and D uses pledge terms and also reverses them, since the borrower would be the pledgor.

questions.question: Before taking a legal mortgage over a plot of land offered as security, a Nigerian bank conducts a search at the land registry (ministry of lands) mainly to

options.a: register the borrower as a customer of the bank
options.b: determine the rate of interest to charge on the loan
options.c: verify the authenticity of the title document and the borrower's ownership
options.d: obtain the borrower's statement of affairs

questions.explanation: The search confirms that the deed or certificate of occupancy is genuine and that the land belongs to the customer, after which a physical inspection checks that the property matches the description. Options B, A and D are not done at the land registry and have nothing to do with confirming title.

questions.question: A promise by one person to answer for the present or future debt of another person, made to the person to whom that other is or will become liable, is a

options.a: Hypothecation
options.b: Guarantee

questions.explanation: A guarantee is a promise by a guarantor (surety) to answer for the debt of the principal debtor to the creditor. Options C, D and A are all rights over goods or property, not promises by a third person to pay another's debt.

questions.question: In a bank guarantee securing a customer's loan, the borrower is referred to as the

options.a: creditor
options.b: surety

questions.explanation: The three parties to a guarantee are the guarantor (or surety), the creditor (the bank) and the principal debtor (the borrower). Options C and B are two names for the same person who gives the promise, and A is the bank.

questions.question: Chief Okoro guarantees his son's overdraft, which rises and falls daily, and the guarantee is to cover not only the present debit balance but any future balance on the account. This is a

options.a: legal mortgage
options.b: continuing guarantee

questions.explanation: A continuing guarantee covers a series of transactions, such as a fluctuating overdraft, including balances arising in future. Option D covers a single debt only, such as one term loan, while A and C are charges over property and goods rather than guarantees.

questions.question: The main weakness of a guarantee as a banking security is that

options.a: it is very difficult and costly to take
options.b: it requires transfer of the legal estate in land
options.c: its value depends wholly on the financial standing of the guarantor
options.d: it can only be used for loans to limited companies

questions.explanation: A guarantee is only as good as the guarantor's ability and willingness to pay, and enforcing it may require costly legal action. Option A is the opposite of the truth, since guarantees are easy to take by simply signing forms. Option D is false because individuals' debts are often guaranteed, and B describes a legal mortgage.

questions.question: A banker's lien differs from an ordinary (particular) lien in that

options.a: the banker may sell the goods after giving proper notice, while an ordinary lienee may only retain them
options.b: the banker may only hold goods that the customer has hypothecated
options.c: the banker must transfer ownership of the goods to himself first
options.d: an ordinary lien gives the creditor ownership of the goods

questions.explanation: A lien is a right to hold the borrower's goods until the debt is paid; under an ordinary lien the creditor can only keep possession, but a banker's lien allows sale after proper notice. Option C is wrong because the customer remains the owner, B confuses lien with hypothecation, and D is wrong because no lien gives ownership.

questions.question: A trader borrows from his bank against bags of rice stored in a warehouse. The bank puts its own padlock on the warehouse door and keeps the key, though the rice is never moved. This arrangement is

options.a: a pledge, with constructive delivery of the goods
options.b: a hypothecation, since the goods were not moved
options.c: a specific guarantee of the trader's debt
options.d: an equitable mortgage of the warehouse

questions.explanation: A pledge is a bailment of goods as security, and delivery can be constructive, for example when the bank puts its lock on the store or takes the key, so possession passes even though the goods stay where they are. Option B is wrong because in hypothecation possession stays with the borrower, while D and C concern land and third-party promises.

questions.question: A charge over goods under which both ownership and possession remain with the borrower, while an equitable charge is created in favour of the bank, is known as

options.a: Pledge
options.b: Lien

questions.explanation: Under hypothecation the borrower keeps the goods and remains the owner, and the bank has an equitable charge plus a right to call for possession when needed. Options A and B both involve the bank holding the goods, and D transfers legal title in land to the lender.

questions.question: Advances against hypothecated goods are considered riskier for a bank than advances against pledged goods because under hypothecation

options.a: the goods must be sold before the loan is granted
options.b: the bank becomes the legal owner of the goods
options.c: no written document is ever signed
options.d: the goods remain in the borrower's possession

questions.explanation: In a pledge the bank holds the goods, but in hypothecation the borrower keeps them, so he could sell or remove them; this is why the bank must check the stock regularly and ask for periodic reports. Option B is false for both arrangements, C is false because a letter or deed of hypothecation is signed, and A makes no sense.

questions.question: Under which of the following does the bank obtain possession of the borrower's goods while the borrower remains their owner?

options.a: Pledge
options.b: Personal guarantee

questions.explanation: A pledge involves delivering the goods, actually or constructively, to the bank as bailee, while ownership stays with the borrower. Option C leaves both ownership and possession with the borrower, B involves no goods at all, and D lets the company keep and trade its assets until crystallisation.

questions.question: A bank takes a charge over all of a manufacturing company's stock-in-trade and receivables, but the company is free to buy and sell these items in the normal course of business until it defaults. This is a

options.a: pledge
options.b: floating charge

questions.explanation: A floating charge covers a class of changing assets, such as stock and receivables, which the company may deal with until the charge crystallises, usually on default or liquidation. Option D attaches to specific identified assets that cannot be disposed of without the lender's consent, C concerns land, and A requires the goods to be delivered to the bank.

questions.question: When a life assurance policy is offered as security, the bank completes a deed of assignment and must then

options.a: give notice of the assignment to the insurance company
options.b: obtain a certificate of occupancy for the policy
options.c: transfer the policy at the stock exchange
options.d: register the policy at the land registry

questions.explanation: Taking a life policy involves checking the insurer's soundness, the beneficiary clause, the surrender value and premium payments, completing a deed of assignment, and giving notice to the insurer, who acknowledges it. Option C applies to shares, while D and B apply to land.

questions.question: When a customer offers quoted shares as security for a loan, the document he signs giving the bank rights over the shares, including the right of disposal on default, is a

options.a: memorandum of deposit
options.b: certificate of occupancy
options.d: deed of assignment of a life policy

questions.explanation: With stocks and shares, the customer signs a memorandum of deposit which gives the bank rights over the shares, including the right to sell them if he defaults. Option B is a title document for land, C is used for goods kept by the borrower, and D is used for life policies.

questions.question: A customer wishes to use his savings account balance as cash security for a loan. Which of the following would he NOT be required to do?

options.a: Issue a letter of authority to transfer money from the account
options.b: Deposit the certificate of occupancy of his house
options.c: Surrender his savings passbook to the bank
options.d: Sign a blank withdrawal form without date and amount

questions.explanation: To pledge a savings balance, the customer gives a letter of authority, surrenders the passbook and signs an undated blank withdrawal form, so the bank can apply the money to the loan. A certificate of occupancy is a land title document and is not part of a cash security. Options A, C and D are all genuine steps.

questions.question: Which of the following documents would a bank require from a corporate loan applicant but NOT from an individual applicant?

options.a: Acceptable security
options.b: Evidence of a current account with the bank

questions.explanation: A certificate of incorporation proves that a company legally exists, so it is required only from corporate customers, along with the memorandum and articles of association and audited accounts. Options C, B and A are required from both individual and corporate applicants.

questions.question: A term loan agreement states that the borrowing company must not create any further charge over its fixed or current assets while the loan is outstanding. This condition is known as

options.a: prohibition of further charges
options.b: rendering of financial returns

questions.explanation: Prohibiting further charges stops other lenders from taking security over the borrower's assets, which protects the lending bank's position. Option D limits dividends and directors' drawings, B requires regular financial statements, and C requires the mortgaged property to be insured.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a usual condition attached to a bank loan agreement?

options.a: Dividends may be restricted until loan repayments are met
options.b: The bank must receive a share of the borrower's annual profits
options.c: The mortgaged property must be insured and kept in good repair
options.d: Major changes in management must be approved by the bank

questions.explanation: Usual loan conditions include prohibition of further charges, approval of management changes, regular financial returns, restriction of benefits to shareholders and insurance cover; a lender earns interest, not a share of profits. Options D, C and A are genuine loan conditions.

questions.question: After a loan has been approved and disbursed, which of the following is a method a bank uses to monitor it?

options.a: Conducting a fresh status enquiry before the application
options.b: Asking the customer to open a current account
options.c: Physical inspection of the project being financed
options.d: Issuing a letter of offer to the customer

questions.explanation: Monitoring after disbursement includes regularly demanding the firm's records, physically inspecting the project and watching how the loan account is conducted. Options A, B and D all belong to the stages before the loan is granted, not to monitoring.

questions.question: The practice where bank lending officers grant loans to their relations or to businesses related to them without applying the basic principles of lending is called

options.a: Credit rationing
options.b: Financial intermediation

questions.explanation: Connected lending, also called insider lending, is lending to persons or businesses linked to bank staff or owners without proper appraisal, and it is a common cause of bad debts. Option D is several banks jointly financing a large loan, A is limiting the amount of credit granted, and B is the general role of banks in channelling funds.

questions.question: A bank lends N30 million against a building valued at N40 million, but when the borrower defaults the building sells for only N22 million because the valuation did not reflect current market prices. The cause of bad debt illustrated is

options.a: changes in economic policies
options.b: connected lending

questions.explanation: Securities that are not valued at current market prices may be overvalued, so on realisation they fail to cover the loan. Option C refers to events such as flood or drought, B to loans to insiders and relations, and A to government policy changes, none of which is described here.

questions.question: Natural hazards such as drought and flood are a cause of bad debts that tends to affect which category of bank loans more than others?

options.a: Overdrafts to salary earners
options.b: Loans secured on cash deposits

questions.explanation: Drought, floods and similar acts of God destroy crops and livestock, so they hit agricultural loans harder than other categories. Options A, B and D are far less exposed to weather, and a loan backed by a cash deposit is largely protected whatever happens.

questions.question: In loan recovery, amicable methods such as restructuring or rescheduling repayments are usually preferred to court action because they

options.a: release all the securities to the borrower
options.b: preserve the banking relationship and avoid costly litigation
options.c: transfer the loan automatically to the CBN
options.d: cancel the borrower's obligation to pay interest

questions.explanation: Amicable recovery, through engagement, restructuring, rescheduling or negotiated settlement, keeps the relationship intact and avoids expensive and slow litigation. Option D is wrong because interest generally remains payable, C has no basis, and A would leave the bank unprotected.

questions.question: Which of the following is a method by which a bank realises its security when a borrower defaults?

options.a: Crediting the loan account with a new loan
options.b: Exercising the power of sale under a mortgage
options.c: Issuing a fresh letter of offer to the borrower
options.d: Conducting a status enquiry on the borrower

questions.explanation: Realisation of security includes exercising the power of sale under a mortgage, appointing a receiver under a debenture, or enforcing a pledge or guarantee, following proper legal procedure. Options C and D belong to the appraisal and approval stage, and A merely adds to the debt without recovering anything.

questions.question: Reporting a defaulting borrower to a licensed credit bureau helps a bank in loan recovery mainly because

options.a: it cancels the borrower's debt to the bank
options.b: it replaces the need for any security on future loans
options.c: it affects the borrower's future access to credit from other lenders
options.d: it transfers ownership of the borrower's assets to the bureau

questions.explanation: Once a default is reported to a credit bureau, other lenders can see it, so the borrower's future access to credit suffers, which encourages repayment. Options A, D and B are not effects of credit bureau reporting; the debt remains owed and the bureau acquires no assets.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way in which a commercial bank extends credit to its customers?

options.a: Loan
options.b: Standing order

questions.explanation: Banks lend through loans, overdrafts and the discounting of bills of exchange. A standing order is an agency service in which the bank makes periodic payments on the customer's instruction, not a form of credit. Options A, D and C are all credit facilities.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a loan from an overdraft?

options.a: On a loan, interest is charged on the whole amount granted; on an overdraft, interest is charged only on the amount actually overdrawn
options.b: A loan is given only to current account holders, while an overdraft can be given to anybody
options.c: A loan is normally short-term, while an overdraft is normally long-term
options.d: On a loan, interest is charged only on the amount used; on an overdraft, interest is charged on the full limit

questions.explanation: A loan is a lump sum placed at the borrower's disposal, so interest runs on the full amount, whereas overdraft interest is charged only on the debit balance actually used. Option D reverses this, B reverses who can obtain each facility, since an overdraft is for current account holders, and C reverses the usual terms.

questions.question: A key difference between a loan and an overdraft is that

options.a: an overdraft requires a separate overdraft account, while a loan runs on the current account
options.b: a loan requires no documentation, while an overdraft requires a great deal
options.c: an overdraft is a lump sum credited to a savings account
options.d: a separate loan account is opened for a loan, while an overdraft runs on the customer's current account

questions.explanation: When a loan is granted the bank opens a separate loan account in the borrower's name, whereas an overdraft is simply the current account being allowed to go into debit up to a limit. Option A reverses the accounts, B reverses the documentation burden, since loans need more documents, and C misdescribes an overdraft.

questions.question: In the banker-customer relationship, a customer who has been granted an overdraft is generally obliged to

options.a: repay only if the bank first obtains a court judgment
options.b: repay only when he chooses to close the account
options.c: repay only at the end of five years
options.d: repay the overdraft on demand when the bank recalls it

questions.explanation: Overdrafts are repayable on demand: the bank may recall the overdraft when it judges this the best course, and the customer is then expected to pay immediately. Options C, A and B wrongly suggest a long fixed term or conditions that would delay repayment.

questions.question: When a bank grants a loan to a customer under normal loan-account practice, the correct entries are to

options.a: credit a new loan account and debit the customer's current account
options.b: debit a new loan account and credit the customer's current account
options.c: debit the customer's current account and credit the bank's cash account
options.d: debit the customer's savings account and credit the bank's capital account

questions.explanation: On granting a loan, a separate loan account is opened and debited with the amount lent, while the customer's current account is credited so he can draw on the funds. Repayments later work the other way, debiting the current account and crediting the loan account. Option A shows the repayment direction, and D and C use the wrong accounts.

questions.question: An arrangement that allows a borrower to retire a loan gradually through periodic payments over its life, rather than paying it all at once at maturity, is known as

options.a: Loan amortisation
options.b: Bullet repayment

questions.explanation: Amortisation spreads repayment of a loan over its life, protecting both lender and borrower against the borrower failing to provide for one large final payment. Option B is the opposite, a single lump-sum repayment at maturity. Option C is several lenders sharing one loan, and D is not a repayment method.

questions.question: Where a loan is taken to purchase a specific asset such as a delivery truck, the amortisation schedule is best designed so that

options.a: the entire principal falls due on the first day of the loan
options.b: repayments continue long after the asset has been scrapped
options.c: repayments match the productive life of the asset and are paid from the cash flows the asset generates
options.d: the borrower pays interest only and never repays the principal

questions.explanation: When a loan finances a specific asset, the repayment schedule should be geared to the asset's productive life, with payments made from the cash flows the asset produces. Option A defeats the purpose of amortisation, B would leave the borrower paying for an asset that no longer earns, and D is not amortisation at all.

questions.question: Mrs Adeyemi borrows N500,000 from her bank for 3 years at 18% per annum flat (simple) interest, calculated on the original principal for the whole period. What is the total interest she pays?
questions.explanation: Flat interest is principal x rate x time = 500,000 x 0.18 x 3 = N270,000. Option C is only one year's interest, B is the total amount repayable (principal plus interest), and A is the result of using only half the period.

questions.question: A trader borrows N1,200,000 for 12 months at 15% per annum flat interest charged on the original principal. Principal and interest are repaid in 12 equal monthly instalments. What is each monthly instalment?
questions.explanation: Flat interest for the year is 1,200,000 x 0.15 x 1 = N180,000, so total repayable is N1,380,000, and 1,380,000 / 12 = N115,000 a month. Option C repays principal only, A is the monthly interest only, and B wrongly adds the whole year's interest to one month's principal.

questions.question: A bank grants Mr Uche a loan of N800,000 repayable in 4 equal half-yearly principal instalments over 2 years, with interest at 12% per annum flat on the original principal paid separately each half-year. Immediately after the third principal instalment is paid, what is the balance of principal on his loan account?
questions.explanation: Each principal instalment is 800,000 / 4 = N200,000, so after three instalments 800,000 - 600,000 = N200,000 remains; interest is paid separately and does not reduce the principal. Option C is the amount already repaid, B is the balance after only two instalments, and D wrongly deducts the three half-yearly interest payments of N48,000 each from the remaining principal.

questions.question: Bisi has a credit balance of N150,000 in her current account when her bank grants her a loan of N600,000, which is credited to that account. The loan is repayable in 3 equal annual principal instalments, with interest at 10% per annum flat on the original principal; each year's principal and interest are debited to her current account. Assuming no other transactions, what is her current account balance immediately after the first year's repayment?

options.a: N550,000 credit
options.b: N370,000 credit

questions.explanation: The account stands at 150,000 + 600,000 = N750,000 after the loan is credited; the first debit is principal 600,000 / 3 = N200,000 plus flat interest 600,000 x 0.10 = N60,000, so 750,000 - 260,000 = N490,000 credit. Option A ignores the interest debit, B wrongly deducts the interest for all three years at once, and D reverses the sign of the balance.

questions.question: A bank lends N1,000,000 at 10% per annum, to be fully amortised by 3 equal annual payments made at the end of each year (annuity method, payment = loan / PVIFA, where PVIFA = [1 - (1.10)^-3] / 0.10). To the nearest kobo, what is each annual payment?
questions.explanation: PVIFA at 10% for 3 years is 2.48685, so the payment is 1,000,000 / 2.48685 = N402,114.80. Option A is the flat-interest figure (1,300,000 / 3), C repays principal only, and B adds just one year's interest to the principal before dividing by 3.

questions.question: A N1,000,000 loan at 10% per annum is amortised by 3 equal end-of-year payments of N402,114.80 each, with interest each year charged on the opening balance. How much of the FIRST payment goes to reduce the principal?
questions.explanation: Interest for year 1 is 10% of the opening balance of N1,000,000, which is N100,000, so the principal reduction is 402,114.80 - 100,000 = N302,114.80. Option D treats the whole payment as principal, B assumes equal principal portions, which happens with equal-principal loans rather than annuities, and A is the interest portion.

questions.question: Kola's current account was overdrawn by N400,000 for 73 days. The bank charges overdraft interest at 20% per annum on the amount overdrawn, using an actual/365 day-count (interest = amount x rate x days / 365). How much interest is charged?
questions.explanation: Interest = 400,000 x 0.20 x 73 / 365 = N16,000. Option A is a full year's interest, C wrongly uses a 360-day year, and B is one month's interest (400,000 x 0.20 / 12), not 73 days.

questions.question: Femi Stores Ltd has an overdraft limit of N1,000,000 but actually overdraws only N600,000, which stays unchanged for 30 days. Interest is charged at 24% per annum on the amount actually overdrawn, actual/365 day-count. To the nearest kobo, what is the interest for the 30 days?
questions.explanation: Overdraft interest is charged on the amount actually overdrawn, so it is 600,000 x 0.24 x 30 / 365 = N11,835.62. Option D wrongly charges interest on the full N1,000,000 limit, C uses a 360-day year, and A is a full year's interest on N600,000.

questions.question: A bank grants a loan of N12 million against a house valued at N20 million. The loan-to-value (LTV) ratio is calculated as loan / value of security x 100. What is the LTV ratio?
questions.explanation: LTV = 12,000,000 / 20,000,000 x 100 = 60%. Option A is the margin as a percentage of the value (the part of the value not lent), B inverts the ratio (value / loan), and C wrongly treats the loan amount in millions as the percentage.

questions.question: A bank's policy allows a maximum loan-to-value ratio of 70% (maximum loan = 70% of the value of the security). A customer offers a plot of land valued at N15 million. What margin, in naira, will the bank keep between the security's value and the maximum loan?
questions.explanation: The maximum loan is 0.70 x 15,000,000 = N10,500,000, so the margin, the excess of the security's value over the loan, is 15,000,000 - 10,500,000 = N4,500,000. Option B is the maximum loan itself, D is the full value of the land, and A misplaces a decimal in the loan figure.

questions.question: Tunde takes a loan of N300,000 for 9 months at 16% per annum flat (simple) interest on the original principal. Using interest = principal x annual rate x (months / 12), how much interest does he pay?
questions.explanation: Interest = 300,000 x 0.16 x 9/12 = N36,000. Option A is a full year's interest, C is just one month's interest, and B wrongly multiplies the annual rate by 9 months instead of 9/12 of a year.

questions.question: A cooperative society borrows N2,000,000 for 2 years at 14% per annum flat interest on the original principal. Principal and total interest are repaid in 8 equal quarterly instalments. What is each quarterly instalment?
questions.explanation: Flat interest is 2,000,000 x 0.14 x 2 = N560,000, so the total repayable is N2,560,000, and 2,560,000 / 8 = N320,000 per quarter. Option A is principal only, B includes only one year's interest, and D wrongly spreads the two years' interest over just 4 quarters.

questions.question: A customer's current account was overdrawn by N250,000 for 20 days and then by N450,000 for the next 10 days. The bank charges 18% per annum on the daily amount actually overdrawn, actual/365 day-count. To the nearest kobo, what is the total overdraft interest for the 30 days?
questions.explanation: Interest is worked out on each balance for the days it was outstanding: 250,000 x 0.18 x 20/365 = N2,465.75 plus 450,000 x 0.18 x 10/365 = N2,219.18, giving N4,684.93. Option C charges the higher balance for all 30 days, B uses a 360-day year, and A charges the lower balance for all 30 days.

questions.question: A bank lends N1,800,000 against quoted shares with a market value of N2,500,000. Expressing the margin (market value of security minus loan) as a percentage of the market value of the security, what is the margin?
questions.explanation: Margin = 2,500,000 - 1,800,000 = N700,000, and 700,000 / 2,500,000 x 100 = 28%. Option A is the loan-to-value ratio rather than the margin, C wrongly divides the margin by the loan instead of the security's value, and B is value divided by loan.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Which of these is NOT an asset to a commercial bank?

options.a: Cash
options.b: Deposits
options.d: Its account balances with other banks

questions.explanation: Deposits are what a bank owes its customers, so they appear on the liabilities side of its balance sheet. Cash (A), loans and advances (C) and balances held with other banks (D) are things the bank owns or is owed, so they are assets. It is tempting to treat deposits as assets because the bank holds the money, but the bank must repay them on demand or at maturity.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Which of the following can be regarded as a liability of a commercial bank?

options.a: Advances
options.b: Deposits

questions.explanation: Deposits are money customers have placed with the bank, so the bank owes that money back to them on demand or at maturity, which makes deposits a liability. Options A and D (advances and overdrafts) are loans the bank has granted to customers, so they are assets, and Option C, treasury bills, are investments the bank holds, which are also assets.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: In managing its portfolio, a commercial bank balances its assets against its liabilities. Which of the following appears on the LIABILITIES side of a commercial bank's balance sheet?

options.a: Investments in treasury bills
options.b: Loans and advances to customers

questions.explanation: Customers' deposits are money the bank owes to its depositors, so they sit on the liabilities side together with shareholders' funds and borrowings from other banks or the central bank. Loans and advances (option B), cash (option D) and investments in treasury bills (option A) are things the bank owns or is owed, so they are assets.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Assets in a bank's balance sheet are usually listed

options.a: in alphabetical order
options.b: in the order in which they were acquired
options.c: in order of liquidity, starting with cash
options.d: in order of size, starting with the largest

questions.explanation: Banks list their assets in order of liquidity, from cash and short-term funds down to fixed assets, which shows how well they can meet depositors' demands. Options A, B and D are not how a bank's balance sheet is set out.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Which asset in a deposit money bank's balance sheet is its main risk asset and generates the bulk of its income?

options.a: Cash and short-term funds
options.b: Treasury bills

questions.explanation: Loans and advances are the credit facilities granted to customers; they carry the most risk and earn most of a bank's income, which is why they attract higher interest and are usually secured by collateral. Option A earns little or nothing, option B is safe and liquid but earns modest returns, and option C covers premises and equipment used in running the bank.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Nigeria's Statement of Accounting Standard (SAS) 10 on accounting by banks focused mainly on

options.a: staff recruitment, training and promotion
options.b: branch location, opening hours and staffing
options.c: allocation of foreign exchange to importers
options.d: income recognition, loss recognition and balance sheet classification

questions.explanation: SAS 10 aimed to make banks' financial statements uniform and reliable by setting rules on when income and losses are recognised and how balance sheet items are classified, partly because profits were thought to be overstated. Options A, B and C are management or policy matters, not accounting standards.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: What is usually the largest liability in the balance sheet of a deposit money bank?

options.a: Customers' deposits
options.b: Share capital

questions.explanation: Deposits from personal and business customers and other banks are the largest liability of a deposit money bank, and much of them can be withdrawn on demand or at short notice. Options B, C and D are also on the liabilities side but are far smaller than deposits.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a liability of a deposit money bank?

options.a: Proposed dividends to shareholders
options.b: Bank drafts issued but not yet paid

questions.explanation: Loans and advances are money owed to the bank by its customers, so they are assets. Options A, B and D are amounts the bank owes to others, so they appear among its liabilities.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-deposit fund of a deposit money bank?

options.a: Current account balances
options.b: Savings account balances

questions.explanation: Retained earnings are profits kept back in the business after dividends are paid, so they come from the bank's own operations rather than from customers' deposits. Options A, B and D are all forms of depositors' funds brought in by customers.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Adebayo Stores Ltd applies to its bank for an overdraft. Its balance sheet shows current assets of N4,800,000 and current liabilities of N3,200,000. What is its current ratio?
questions.explanation: The current ratio is current assets divided by current liabilities, so 4,800,000 / 3,200,000 = 1.5 : 1. Option C turns the ratio upside down (liabilities over assets), while B and D do not follow from the figures given.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Adebayo Stores Ltd has current assets of N4,800,000 (including stock of N1,600,000) and current liabilities of N3,200,000. What is its quick (acid-test) ratio?
questions.explanation: The quick ratio removes stock from current assets because stock is the least liquid current asset: (4,800,000 - 1,600,000) / 3,200,000 = 1.0 : 1. Option D is the current ratio, which forgets to deduct stock, and B divides stock alone by current liabilities.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Chinedu Ventures has current assets of N7,500,000 and current liabilities of N5,250,000. What is its working capital?
questions.explanation: Working capital (net current assets) is current assets minus current liabilities: 7,500,000 - 5,250,000 = N2,250,000. Option C adds the two figures instead of subtracting, and D subtracts the wrong way round, giving a negative figure.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Gearing is defined here as long-term debt divided by (long-term debt + shareholders' funds). Okon Plastics Ltd has long-term loans of N6,000,000 and shareholders' funds of N14,000,000. Its gearing is
questions.explanation: With the stated definition, gearing = 6,000,000 / (6,000,000 + 14,000,000) = 30%. Option D (42.9%) is the debt-to-equity ratio, which divides debt by equity only, and B is the share of total long-term funds supplied by the owners rather than by lenders.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Bello Agro Ltd has total long-term debt of N9,000,000 and shareholders' equity of N12,000,000. What is its debt-to-equity ratio?
questions.explanation: Debt-to-equity is debt divided by equity: 9,000,000 / 12,000,000 = 0.75 : 1, meaning lenders supply 75 kobo for every naira the owners have put in. Option C divides equity by debt, and B is debt as a share of debt plus equity (a gearing-type measure).

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Ifeoma Foods Ltd earned profit before interest and tax of N8,400,000 and paid loan interest of N1,200,000 for the year. What is its interest cover?

options.a: 8.4 times
options.b: 0.14 times

questions.explanation: Interest cover is profit before interest and tax divided by interest charges: 8,400,000 / 1,200,000 = 7 times. Option C wrongly deducts the interest from profit first, and B inverts the ratio.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: A Lagos pharmacy recorded sales of N24,000,000 and a net profit of N1,800,000 for the year. Its net profit margin is
questions.explanation: Net profit margin is net profit divided by sales, times 100: 1,800,000 / 24,000,000 x 100 = 7.5%. Option D divides sales by profit (13.3 times), and C misplaces the decimal point.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Emeka Motors Ltd has shareholders' funds of N15,000,000 and long-term loans of N5,000,000, and earned profit before interest and tax of N3,600,000. Taking capital employed as shareholders' funds plus long-term loans, its return on capital employed (ROCE) is
questions.explanation: ROCE = PBIT / capital employed = 3,600,000 / (15,000,000 + 5,000,000) = 18%. Option A uses shareholders' funds alone as the denominator, and D uses only the long-term loans.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Ngozi Textiles holds closing stock of N2,400,000. Its cost of sales for the year was N14,600,000 and its sales were N21,900,000. Using a 365-day year and cost of sales, how many days' stock does it hold?

options.a: 6.1 days
options.b: 60 days

questions.explanation: Stock days = stock / cost of sales x 365 = 2,400,000 / 14,600,000 x 365 = 60 days. Option D wrongly uses sales instead of cost of sales, and A is the stock turnover in times (about 6.1), not a number of days.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Kunle Distributors has trade debtors of N3,000,000 and annual credit sales of N18,250,000. Using a 365-day year, its debtor collection period is

options.a: 30 days
options.b: 6.1 days

questions.explanation: Debtor days = debtors / credit sales x 365 = 3,000,000 / 18,250,000 x 365 = 60 days, so customers take about two months to pay. Option B is the debtor turnover in times (18,250,000 / 3,000,000), not days.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Halima Supermarket's cost of sales was N18,000,000 and its average stock was N3,000,000. What is its stock turnover?

options.a: 21 times
options.b: 0.17 times

questions.explanation: Stock turnover = cost of sales / average stock = 18,000,000 / 3,000,000 = 6 times a year, meaning stock is replaced roughly every two months. Option B inverts the ratio, and A wrongly adds the two figures before dividing.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Tunde Hardware's balance sheet shows: stock N2,000,000; debtors N1,500,000; cash N500,000; trade creditors N1,600,000; bank overdraft N900,000. What is its current ratio?
questions.explanation: Current assets are 2,000,000 + 1,500,000 + 500,000 = 4,000,000 and current liabilities are 1,600,000 + 900,000 = 2,500,000, so the current ratio is 1.6 : 1. Option C forgets that the bank overdraft is a current liability, and A is the quick ratio because it leaves out stock.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: A customer's current ratio is 1.2 : 1 and its current liabilities are N5,000,000. What is its working capital?
questions.explanation: Current assets are 1.2 x 5,000,000 = 6,000,000, so working capital = 6,000,000 - 5,000,000 = N1,000,000. Option D is the current assets figure, not working capital, and C wrongly divides the liabilities by the ratio.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Ada Cosmetics had sales of N40,000,000, gross profit of N12,000,000 and operating expenses of N7,000,000 (ignore tax and interest). What is its net profit margin?
questions.explanation: Net profit is gross profit minus expenses, 12,000,000 - 7,000,000 = 5,000,000, and 5,000,000 / 40,000,000 = 12.5%. Option D is the gross profit margin, and C is the expenses-to-sales ratio.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Taking the liquidity ratio as liquid assets divided by total deposit liabilities, a deposit money bank with liquid assets of N36 billion and total deposits of N120 billion has a liquidity ratio of
questions.explanation: Liquidity ratio = 36 / 120 x 100 = 30%, showing what share of deposits could be met from liquid assets. Option D inverts the ratio (3.33 times written as a percentage), and A is the share of deposits not covered by liquid assets.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Assume the Central Bank sets a cash reserve ratio of 20% on deposits. A bank with eligible deposits of N250 billion must keep a cash reserve with the Central Bank of

options.a: N50 billion
options.b: N12.5 billion

questions.explanation: The required cash reserve is deposits x cash reserve ratio = 250 x 0.20 = N50 billion. Option C is the amount left after the reserve, and D wrongly divides deposits by 0.20 instead of multiplying.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: A bank has loans and advances of N84 billion and total customer deposits of N120 billion. Its loan-to-deposit ratio is
questions.explanation: Loan-to-deposit ratio = loans / deposits x 100 = 84 / 120 = 70%, meaning 70 kobo of every naira deposited has been lent out. Option A divides deposits by loans, and D is the share of deposits not lent out.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Assume a cash reserve ratio of 25%. A bank has deposits of N200 billion and currently holds N56 billion with the Central Bank. Its excess reserve is

options.a: N6 billion
options.b: N42 billion

questions.explanation: Required reserve = 25% x 200 = N50 billion, so excess = 56 - 50 = N6 billion. Option D is the required reserve itself, and C is deposits minus the amount held.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: A bank's assets are: cash N5bn, balances with the Central Bank N12bn, treasury bills N18bn, loans and advances N90bn, fixed assets N10bn. Its deposits are N140bn. Treating cash, Central Bank balances and treasury bills as liquid assets, its liquidity ratio is
questions.explanation: Liquid assets = 5 + 12 + 18 = N35bn, and 35 / 140 = 25%. Option C wrongly counts loans and advances (which are risk assets, not liquid assets) and A counts only cash and Central Bank balances, leaving out treasury bills.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Under BOFIA 2020, a bank whose statutory reserve fund is less than its paid-up share capital reports net profit after tax of N8 billion. The minimum it must transfer to the statutory reserve before declaring a dividend is

options.a: N0.8 billion
options.b: N1.2 billion

questions.explanation: Where the reserve fund is below paid-up capital, at least 30% of net profit after tax goes to the reserve: 30% x 8 = N2.4 billion. Option B applies the 15% rate, which is used only once the reserve fund equals or exceeds paid-up capital.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Under BOFIA 2020, a bank's statutory reserve fund already exceeds its paid-up share capital. If its net profit after tax is N12 billion, the minimum transfer to the statutory reserve is

options.a: N3.6 billion
options.b: N1.8 billion

questions.explanation: Once the reserve fund equals or exceeds paid-up capital, the minimum transfer falls to 15% of net profit: 15% x 12 = N1.8 billion. Option A uses the 30% rate, which applies only while the reserve fund is still below paid-up capital.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Femi Bakeries reports profit before tax of N5,400,000 after charging loan interest of N600,000. What is its interest cover?

options.a: 9 times
options.b: 0.1 times

questions.explanation: Interest cover uses profit BEFORE interest and tax, so first add the interest back: 5,400,000 + 600,000 = 6,000,000, then 6,000,000 / 600,000 = 10 times. Option A uses profit before tax without adding back the interest, and B inverts the ratio.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Gearing is defined here as long-term debt divided by (long-term debt + shareholders' funds). Uche Haulage Ltd has share capital of N15,000,000, retained profits of N6,000,000 and a long-term bank loan of N9,000,000. Its gearing is
questions.explanation: Shareholders' funds are share capital plus retained profits, 15,000,000 + 6,000,000 = 21,000,000, so gearing = 9,000,000 / (9,000,000 + 21,000,000) = 30%. Option C forgets the retained profits and uses share capital alone, and A is the debt-to-equity ratio (9 / 21).

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: A bank with customer deposits of N300 billion has an internal policy that its loan-to-deposit ratio must not exceed 65%. What is the maximum amount of loans and advances it can hold?

options.a: N195 billion
options.b: N235 billion

questions.explanation: Maximum loans = deposits x 65% = 300 x 0.65 = N195 billion. Option C is the 35% of deposits that must stay unlent, and D wrongly divides deposits by 0.65.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Assume a minimum liquidity ratio of 30% of deposits. A bank with deposits of N500 billion holds liquid assets of N135 billion. By how much is it short of the minimum?

options.a: N3 billion
options.b: N15 billion

questions.explanation: The bank needs 30% x 500 = N150 billion of liquid assets but holds 135, so it is N15 billion short. Option C is the full requirement rather than the shortfall, and D is deposits minus liquid assets held.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: In the balance sheet of a deposit money bank, assets are normally arranged

options.a: in order of liquidity, starting with cash
options.b: in alphabetical order of the asset names
options.c: in order of the dates on which they were acquired
options.d: in order of size, starting with the largest

questions.explanation: Banks group assets by nature and list them in order of liquidity and maturity, so the reader can see at a glance whether the bank holds enough cash and liquid assets to repay depositors at short notice. Options D, B and C would hide that liquidity picture.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Which of the following assets of a deposit money bank is the MOST liquid?

options.a: Loans and advances
options.b: Fixed assets such as land and buildings

questions.explanation: Cash and short-term funds (currency held in the strong rooms and cheques due from other banks) are already money or very close to it, so they head the asset side. Loans and advances in option A are risk assets tied up with borrowers, and fixed assets in B are the hardest to turn into cash.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: On a deposit money bank's balance sheet, the item described as the bank's 'risk assets', from which about seventy percent or more of its revenue comes, is

options.a: bills discounted
options.b: loans and advances

questions.explanation: Loans and advances are the credit facilities granted to customers; they earn the highest interest but carry default risk, which is why bankers take security. Treasury bills in option D are near-riskless government paper, and cash in C earns nothing.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Banks hold treasury bills as a short-term investment mainly because they

options.a: earn the highest rate of interest of all bank assets
options.b: never mature and so provide a permanent income
options.c: are secured on the borrower's land and buildings
options.d: are safe, highly liquid and can be rediscounted with the Central Bank before maturity

questions.explanation: Treasury bills are short government securities (commonly 91 days) that are low-risk and can be rediscounted with the Central Bank of Nigeria if the bank needs cash early. Option A describes loans and advances, which pay more because they are riskier, and C describes a secured loan, not a government bill.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an item under 'other liabilities' in a deposit money bank's balance sheet?

options.a: Provision for taxation
options.b: Proposed dividends to shareholders

questions.explanation: Accrued interest receivable is money owed TO the bank, so it is grouped under other assets. Provision for taxation, proposed dividends and outstanding bank drafts/certified cheques (options A, B, D) are all amounts the bank owes and appear under other liabilities.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Deposits are described as the largest liability of a deposit money bank because

options.a: deposits are reserves the law requires the bank to set aside from profit
options.b: depositors are creditors of the bank who can call for most of their money on demand or at short notice
options.c: deposits are the bank's own capital contributed by shareholders
options.d: deposits are loans the bank has granted to its customers

questions.explanation: A deposit is money the bank owes back to the customer, making the depositor a creditor, and deposits are by far the biggest part of the money a bank works with. Option C describes capital, D describes loans and advances (an asset), and A describes the statutory reserve.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Mr Eze has N2,000,000 in his current account and his neighbour Mrs Musa has an overdraft of N500,000 with the same bank. In the bank's balance sheet,

options.a: both balances are liabilities of the bank
options.b: Mr Eze's balance is an asset and Mrs Musa's overdraft is a liability
options.c: both balances are assets of the bank
options.d: Mr Eze's balance is a liability and Mrs Musa's overdraft is an asset

questions.explanation: A credit balance is money the bank owes the customer, so it is a deposit liability, while an overdraft is money the customer owes the bank, so it is part of loans and advances on the asset side. Option B reverses the two, which is the usual mistake of looking at it from the customer's side.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three main areas of bank accounting practice addressed by Statement of Accounting Standard (SAS) 10?

options.a: Foreign exchange rate determination
options.b: Income recognition

questions.explanation: SAS 10 on banks and similar institutions deals with income recognition, loss recognition and balance sheet classification, aiming to make bank accounts reliable and comparable. Setting foreign exchange rates is a monetary-policy and market matter, not an accounting standard area.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: A major reason for a specific accounting standard (SAS 10) for banks in Nigeria was

options.a: inconsistent accounting policies and allegedly overstated bank profits that made comparison of performance difficult
options.b: the need to fix the interest rate banks pay on savings accounts
options.c: the need to stop banks from granting loans and advances
options.d: the need to replace the balance sheet with a cash book

questions.explanation: SAS 10 was a response to inconsistent policies, overstated profits and the need to keep public confidence in banks, so that bank statements would be uniform and comparable. Options B, C and D are not accounting-standard purposes at all.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Under BOFIA 2020, the statutory reserve fund of a bank is built up by transferring a percentage of

options.a: gross income, before tax and expenses
options.b: total deposits, at the end of each month
options.c: net profit after tax, before any dividend is declared
options.d: paid-up capital, whenever new shares are issued

questions.explanation: The Act requires every bank to transfer part of its net profits for the year, after provision for tax and before any dividend, into a statutory reserve fund (30% while the fund is below paid-up capital, 15% once it equals or exceeds it). Option B confuses this with the cash reserve held against deposits at the Central Bank.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: In a bank's balance sheet, 'retained profits' (retained earnings) are

options.a: profits paid out to shareholders as dividends
options.b: interest paid to depositors during the year
options.c: undivided profits left in the business after dividends and all other appropriations
options.d: the maximum share capital the bank may issue

questions.explanation: Retained profits are accumulated net income kept in the bank after dividends and other appropriations, and they form part of shareholders' funds. Option A is the opposite (profit distributed), and D describes authorised capital.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Which of the following appears on the ASSETS side of a bank's balance sheet?

options.a: Proposed dividends
options.b: Statutory reserves

questions.explanation: Bills discounted (treasury bills, trade bills, bankers' acceptances and commercial papers bought by the bank) are claims the bank holds, so they are assets. Statutory reserves (option B) are part of shareholders' funds, while deposits and proposed dividends (D, A) are amounts the bank owes.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: A bank's land and buildings, vehicles, computers and other equipment, shown in the balance sheet at cost less depreciation, are classified as

options.a: other assets
options.b: equipment on lease

questions.explanation: Fixed assets are the bank's own premises and equipment, shown at their net value after periodic depreciation. Option A covers items such as prepayments and accrued interest, C covers stocks and bonds, and B covers assets the bank has leased out to customers.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: A bank issues a performance guarantee for a customer who is building a road for a state government. Until the customer defaults, this guarantee is

options.a: an off-balance-sheet (contingent) item disclosed in the notes to the accounts
options.b: a deposit liability shown in the balance sheet
options.c: part of the bank's statutory reserve
options.d: a loan and advance shown as an asset

questions.explanation: Guarantees, bonds, acceptances and letters of credit only become real debts if a stated event happens, so they are contingent liabilities disclosed alongside, but not in, the balance sheet. No money has been lent or deposited, so options B and D are wrong.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Compared with the balance sheet of a trading company, a commercial bank's balance sheet typically shows

options.a: no current liabilities because deposits are permanent capital
options.b: mainly stock and fixed assets funded largely by shareholders' capital
options.c: mainly financial assets funded largely by deposits, with fixed assets forming a small share
options.d: loans and advances on the liabilities side

questions.explanation: A bank deals in money: its assets are mostly cash, securities and loans, and most of its funds come from depositors, so it is very highly geared compared with a trading firm. Option B describes a trading or manufacturing company, and A is wrong because most deposits are repayable on demand or at short notice.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: Which of the following is a NON-DEPOSIT source of funds for a deposit money bank?

options.a: Savings account deposits
options.b: Fixed (time) deposits
options.d: Rental income from bank property let to others

questions.explanation: Non-deposit funds include investment income, rental income, borrowing, owners' capital, retained earnings, fees and sale of assets. Options A, C and B are all depositors' funds brought in by customers.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
questions.question: In the classification of bank deposits, current account balances are best described as

options.a: funds from investors seeking money market yields
options.b: deposits with a fixed maturity and stipulated rate of interest
options.c: deposits that bear the lowest rate of interest and need a minimal opening amount
options.d: non-interest-bearing demand deposits that can be withdrawn at any time by cheque

questions.explanation: Current account money can be drawn at any time without notice, usually by cheque, and normally earns no interest. Option B describes fixed (time) deposits, and C describes savings accounts.

questions.topic: Balance Sheet Structure and Interpreting Customers' Accounts
